Tetragon can also act in the kernel, which the [enforcing policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/tetragon/index.md#enforcement>) uses to kill a container that creates a user namespace. The cost is a smaller rule library: every `TracingPolicy` here was written for this cluster.

# GitOps Strategy

ArgoCD manages the cluster state declaratively: if it is not in Git, it is not in the cluster, and if you put it there anyway the next reconcile puts it back.

## Structure

```
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Bootstrap (once, by hand)"
        PJ[payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml]
        AA[payload/argocd/application.yaml]
    end

    AA --> AR[Application argocd]
    AS --> |"payload/argocd/application.yaml"| AR
    AR --> |"argo-cd chart + values.yaml"| SELF[ArgoCD itself]
    AR --> |"payload/argocd/applicationset-platform.yaml"| AS[ApplicationSet platform]
    AS --> |"payload/platform/*/application.yaml"| INFRA[Every component]
    AS --> |"payload/workloads/application.yaml"| WA[Application workloads]
    WA --> |"payload/workloads/applicationset.yaml"| APPS[ApplicationSet apps]
    APPS --> |"homelab-apps: */application.yaml"| WL[Every workload]
```

`argocd` is applied by hand once, at bootstrap, and the `platform` ApplicationSet it deploys then adopts it from `payload/argocd/application.yaml`, so a merged chart bump reaches the cluster like any other. It syncs the chart that runs ArgoCD and, through a second source, the `platform` ApplicationSet, so changes to the generator arrive through Git. Its chart values and the recovery commands are in [Platform → ArgoCD](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md>).

Everything else is a component directory with one `application.yaml`, including ArgoCD's own supporting resources:

| Application | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `argocd-projects` | the `apps`, `infra` and `system` AppProjects, and a locked `default` so an Application that names no project can do nothing |
| `argocd-config` | the `ExternalSecret` for ArgoCD's OIDC client, and its Grafana dashboard; the routes are the chart's, in `payload/argocd/values.yaml` |

An Application naming a project that does not exist is rejected, so `payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml` is applied once at bootstrap, ahead of the `argocd` Application that names `system`, and `argocd-projects` adopts it on its first sync. A broken project definition is fixed with `kubectl apply`, not a sync.

Each `application.yaml` is a complete Application: the generator copies its labels, annotations, finalizers and `spec` unchanged.

## Sync policy

Every Application, generated or not, carries the same `syncPolicy`: automated sync with `prune` and `selfHeal`, and a `retry` block:

- **A commit is live within one polling interval.** ArgoCD runs on a private address, so no GitHub webhook can reach it; the intervals are in [Platform → ArgoCD](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md#configuration>).
- **Drift is reverted.** A resource edited or deleted by hand is put back on the next reconcile, in the platform as much as in the workloads.
- **A failed sync retries itself.** ArgoCD never re-attempts a failed sync of the same revision unless the Application has a `retry` block, which is why every `application.yaml` carries one. Once its attempts run out the Application stays OutOfSync until its revision changes or it is synced by hand:

  ```bash
  argocd app sync <application>
  ```
- **Patching a generated Application's `spec` achieves nothing.** The next ApplicationSet reconcile copies the file back over it. That includes switching automated sync off: the only rollback is a revert commit — see [Rolling back a bad sync](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/troubleshooting/index.md#rolling-back-a-bad-sync>).
- **`argocd` carries no finalizer.** The ApplicationSet deletes a generated Application whose file or generator path goes away, and with the resources finalizer that would delete ArgoCD itself; without it the objects stay.
- **One exception to `prune`, and one annotation.** `kube-vip` syncs with `prune: false`, because its objects are the only thing holding the API VIP; copy the `syncPolicy` from any other sibling. Elsewhere a resource whose deletion would take more than itself carries a per-resource `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false` instead: a Namespace (everything in it), an AppProject (every Application in it is orphaned), a CloudNativePG `Cluster` and the bucket its backups land in. A removed policy or manifest still prunes; the container it lived in stays.

## Bootstrap convergence

Nothing orders the Applications. On a fresh cluster the ApplicationSet generates all of them at once and they converge on their own: a sync that fails because a kind does not exist yet is retried once the chart that ships it has landed, and a resource that applies but cannot go Ready waits without failing anything. What each component waits for is in [Platform → Rollout order](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/index.md#rollout-order>).

| While it is missing | The dependent Application | Resolves when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A CRD (`ServiceMonitor`, `HTTPRoute`, `ExternalSecret`, a Rook or CNPG kind) | fails its sync and retries | the chart shipping the CRD has synced |
| A `StorageClass` | is Progressing, its pods Pending | `rook-ceph-cluster` reports Ready |
| A working `ClusterSecretStore` | is Degraded on every `ExternalSecret` | OpenBao is unsealed and holds the key |
| A Gateway to attach to | is Progressing on every `HTTPRoute` | `gateway-api` holds its certificates |

Two placement rules keep this convergence short. **A resource lives with what it needs, not with what it configures:** the `ClusterSecretStore` is in `openbao`, not `external-secrets`, and cert-manager's issuers and certificates are their own `certificates` Application, so the controllers report Healthy on their own and the resources that wait for OpenBao are the ones that say so. **A resource that fails to apply for longer than the retry budget belongs elsewhere:** the budget covers a chart arriving minutes late, not a human.

### Bootstrap pauses at OpenBao

A fresh cluster looks stuck at OpenBao by design. OpenBao's pods report Ready while sealed, but the `ClusterSecretStore` beside it stays Degraded until OpenBao is initialised, unsealed and has the Kubernetes auth role, and with it every `ExternalSecret` in the platform. `make bao-init` clears that, and `make bao-unseal` after every later restart; `certificates` then waits for `make bao-secrets` to write the Route53 credentials, and the Gateways for the certificates. Nothing fails: every one of those resources applied cleanly and is waiting on status.

## Workloads live in a second repository

The applications the cluster exists to run are in [`JanWelker/homelab-apps`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps>), one directory per application; the `apps` ApplicationSet generates an Application from each `*/application.yaml` there. The split keeps a platform change with a cluster-wide blast radius apart from a workload change with a one-app one.

Workloads reference the platform: the `apps-gateway`, the `rook-ceph-block` StorageClass, the `openbao` `ClusterSecretStore`, the CloudNativePG operator. The platform names the workloads repository in the `apps` ApplicationSet and the `apps` project, and single workloads wherever it grants them something. A fork with other workloads edits these, in `payload/platform/` or `scripts/`; `git grep <namespace>` finds the rest:

| File | Names |
| --- | --- |
| `openbao/cluster-secret-store.yaml`, `scripts/bao-policies.sh` | secret readers |
| `authentik/` blueprints, secrets, `referencegrant.yaml` | login clients, proxied hostnames |
| `gateway-api/gateways.yaml`, `security/admission-policies.yaml` | `infra-gateway` namespaces, reserved hostnames |
| `security/` pod security, network policies, agent RBAC | labels, flows, agent access |
| `scripts/bao-secrets.sh` | typed secrets |

### What the split costs

- **Two repositories to clone**, and a change that spans both is two pull requests that cannot merge atomically; merge the platform half first.
- **A workload can reference a missing platform resource**; nothing catches it before the sync.

### Workloads sync alongside the platform

The `apps` ApplicationSet ships inside the `workloads` Application, which the `platform` ApplicationSet generates like any component, from a second generator path beside the `payload/platform/` glob.

On a fresh cluster the workloads therefore start syncing before the platform under them is Healthy and [converge the same way](<#bootstrap-convergence>). Ordering *within* a workload uses resource-level sync waves — the CloudNativePG `Cluster` is in an earlier wave, and ArgoCD's built-in health check for `postgresql.cnpg.io/Cluster` waits for it before applying the application.

## Moving a resource to another Application

Moving a manifest between directories is not a move to ArgoCD: the old Application sees a tracked resource vanish and, with `prune: true`, deletes it; the new one recreates it, possibly seconds later. For a `ClusterSecretStore` that is an outage of every secret; for a child `Application` with the resources finalizer it deletes everything that Application deployed. A move takes two merges:

1. Annotate the resource where it is, and let that sync:

   ```yaml
   annotations:
     argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false
     argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: IgnoreExtraneous
   ```

   Both are read off the **live** object. `Prune=false` stops whichever Application prunes first; `IgnoreExtraneous` keeps the old Application Synced while it still sees the resource. 2. Move the file, keeping the annotations. The new Application takes over the tracking annotation.

The annotations can go once the second change has synced.

## Version pins

Each chart version is pinned once, in the `application.yaml` that owns the component, or in the `kustomization.yaml` beside it for a chart that needs a post-render, which Argo CD's Helm source cannot do: Kustomize's `helmCharts` renders it, enabled by `kustomize.buildOptions` in `argocd-cm`. The node-level versions (Flatcar, Kubernetes, syslinux) are pinned once in `ansible/inventory.yaml`. The `Makefile` reads `targetRevision` for `make install-cilium` and `make install-argo`, so bootstrap installs what ArgoCD then reconciles. kube-vip is the one double pin: `kube_vip_version` in the inventory for the bootstrap static pod, and the image in `payload/platform/kube-vip/daemonset.yaml` for what runs after the first sync. Renovate tracks all of them; its automerge policy is in [Maintenance](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md>).

# Known Limitations

Things this cluster does not do. None is a bug; each is an accepted tradeoff or work not yet done.

| Limitation | Consequence | Mitigation / plan | Where documented |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **The API endpoint address is fixed at `kubeadm init`** | The kube-vip VIP is baked into the API server certificates, every kubeconfig and Cilium's `k8sServiceHost`; moving it touches every node | Choose it once, outside any DHCP range and the LoadBalancer pools; the next build [uses a name](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/index.md#endpoint-name>) | [Choosing the address](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/index.md#choosing-the-address>), [migrating in place](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/index.md#in-place>) |
| **OpenBao needs an operator to unseal it** | Every restart seals it until the [threshold of key shares](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#at-a-glance>) is supplied; sealed, no `ExternalSecret` resolves and certificates silently stop renewing | Check `bao status` after reboots; auto-unseal would add an external dependency | [Unsealing after a restart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#unsealing-after-a-restart>), [after any node reboot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#after-any-node-reboot-unseal-openbao>) |
| **One operator holds every credential** | The unseal key shares and `output/credentials/` sit with one person, on the deployment host | Copy them to a password manager | [Bootstrap](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#bootstrap>), [Repository layout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/index.md#repository-layout>) |
| **Alerting reaches one mailbox** | A rejected mail, an expired SMTP password or a Ceph outage ([Prometheus and Alertmanager](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md#at-a-glance>) sit on Ceph) stops alerts silently; `Watchdog` proves only as far as Alertmanager | An off-cluster `Watchdog` mail check; meanwhile, the routine health check | [Alerting](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md#alerting>), [routine health check](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/index.md#routine-health-check>) |
| **Automatic updates stop at patch releases** | Nodes follow the Kubernetes minor they were built with; a minor upgrade is manual | By design | [Nodes are pinned to a minor series](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/index.md#nodes-are-pinned-to-a-minor-series>), [upgrading a minor deliberately](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/index.md#upgrading-a-minor-version-deliberately>), [Kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) |
| **The `infra` AppProject is permissive** | The `infra` AppProject allows every kind in every namespace, so a platform `application.yaml` can deploy anything anywhere | Narrow the projects | [Security Posture](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/security/index.md#authorization>) |
| **Reprovisioning needs the boot server on the segment** | Rebuilding a node needs `make serve` on the nodes' L2 segment, the DHCP pointing at it and a power cycle; there is no remote rebuild | A running node reboots and rejoins without it | [Boot & Bootstrap Process](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/index.md#every-boot-after-the-first>) |
| **The object store survives one host down, no more** | During every Kured reboot the RGW data pool, which holds the backups and Loki chunks, has no redundancy left, while `rbd-pool` still has some | Accepted: a pool's erasure profile is fixed, so fixing it means a new pool and moving every bucket | [Object storage](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md#object-storage>) |
| **Cluster admin is a client certificate, not OIDC** | `output/kubeconfig` is `admin.conf`, a certificate only a CA rotation revokes; the API server has no OIDC | Accepted: one operator, LAN-only API | [Authorization](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/security/index.md#authorization>) |
| **OpenBao speaks plain HTTP inside the cluster** | Secrets and tokens cross the pod network unencrypted; WireGuard covers node-to-node | Accepted: a certificate would sit in the unseal path | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#at-a-glance>) |
| **OSDs are unencrypted, the Rook toolbox is on, Loki has no tenants** | A pulled disk is readable; the toolbox is a standing Ceph admin shell; any Grafana Viewer reads every log line, the audit log included | Accepted: disks stay on site, runbooks need the toolbox, one Grafana user | [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>), [Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) |
| **SELinux is permissive on every node** | Flatcar's default: SELinux does not mediate a container escape, and Tetragon detects without confining | The denials are answered; enforce on one worker first | [Node hardening](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/security/index.md#node-hardening>) |
| **Ceph's daemons run privileged** | `hostpathRequiresPrivileged`, Rook's switch for SELinux hosts: `container_t` may not write their hostPath data. A privileged container has every capability and no seccomp filter | Accepted until the paths carry a label | [Rook Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md#selinux>) |
| **The `infra` hostnames and the LAN address are in public DNS** | The infra names resolve publicly to a LAN address, so anyone can list them; they stay LAN-only | Accepted: no split DNS to run | [external-dns](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-dns/index.md>) |
| **Single region, site and rack** | Ceph replicates across nodes on one power feed and TrueNAS pulls the backups over the same LAN ([Off-cluster copy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md#off-cluster-copy>)), so a site-level event takes everything | Honest limit of a homelab: a copy off the site | — |
| **No staging cluster** | A merge to `main` is a production deployment | The pull request checks and diff preview | [Contributing](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/contributing/index.md>) |
| **The router and Authentik stand alone** | The router carries every Internet request and the BGP sessions; Authentik every UI login | LAN clients still reach the Gateways over L2 | [Cilium](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cilium/index.md#configuration>), [When Authentik is down](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md#when-authentik-is-down>) |
| **Backup copies hold plaintext Secrets and one all-powerful key** | Velero's resource backups keep Secrets as plain JSON, and the NAS's `offsite-reader` key owns the bucket, so a leak of either exposes every Secret or the backups themselves | Accepted; the NAS's snapshots outlive a deletion | [Repository password](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/index.md#repository-password>), [Off-cluster reader](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md#off-cluster-reader>) |

# Security Posture

This is a homelab on a private network, and several deliberate shortcuts follow from that. They are listed so a reader can tell a decision from an oversight.

## Assumed trust boundary

The cluster assumes a **trusted L2 network segment**: anything with a port on it is treated as friendly. There is no VPN requirement and no mutual TLS between components; inside the cluster, the default-deny network policies in [Authorization](<#authorization>) are the segmentation.

One surface faces the Internet: the router forwards ports 80 and 443 to `apps-gateway`, whose names external-dns publishes on the public address — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md#configuration>). The `infra` names resolve publicly too, since the DNS-01 challenge needs a public zone, and sit in Certificate Transparency logs, but point at a LAN address.

## Provisioning

Provisioning is the least protected phase: it runs before any of the cluster's own security exists.

| Property | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Ignition configs travel over plain HTTP | The boot server gives `ignition-<host>.json` only to that host's `ansible_host`, and the installer config pins its sha512. A LAN host that forges the address or sits in between still reads it |
| Those configs embed join credentials | The bootstrap `token`, and on control-plane nodes the `certificateKey`, together enough to join a new control-plane node. Only the init host has them in its kubeadm config; the others get a `0600` environment file that `bootstrap-k8s.service` names by variable. The service deletes both files once the node has joined, so neither `systemctl show` nor the disk keeps them |
| The control-plane configs embed the etcd encryption key | `/etc/kubernetes/enc/encryption-config.yaml` is inlined with the key that encrypts every Secret at rest. It has no TTL: whoever fetched a control-plane config can read Secrets out of any etcd backup for the life of the cluster |
| Nodes join with `--discovery-token-unsafe-skip-ca-verification` | A joining node does not verify the API server's CA |
| Sysext updates set `Verify=false` | On first boot Ignition checks each image against the sha256 the boot server was given, so a substituted image fails. Later sysupdate downloads travel over HTTPS with signature verification off; the transfer config naming their source is inlined from Git, not fetched |
| The PXE kernel, initrd and bootloader are signature-checked | `make download` takes their sums only from a clearsigned file that `gpgv` verifies against a pinned key fingerprint: Flatcar's image signing key for `.DIGESTS.asc`, kernel.org's autosigner for syslinux's `sha256sums.asc` |
| The OS image is signature-checked | `flatcar-install` is given `-b`/`-V`, so the node downloads the image and its detached signature and checks both against Flatcar's key before writing anything |

The mitigation is time: `make serve` is a foreground command, the bootstrap token and the certificate key expire (the windows are in [Switching back to local boot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/index.md#switching-back-to-local-boot>)), and `make config` re-arms both only for those windows, over SSH through a script's stdin, so no process list shows them. The encryption key has no clock, which is why HTTP listens only on `boot_server_ip`, serves files by name and lists nothing. TFTP listens on every interface, since macOS lets an unprivileged process bind port 69 only there, and refuses every write request, so nobody can plant a boot menu. **Stop the boot server when provisioning is finished.** Flatcar is installed to disk and nothing needs it after a build — see [Every boot after the first](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/index.md#every-boot-after-the-first>).

`output/credentials/` holds the generated bootstrap token and certificate key in plaintext. The directory is `0700`, the Ignition configs in `output/http` are `0600`, and `output/` is gitignored. The values are reused across `make config` runs, because a node whose join window passed retries with the values on its disk once `make config` has re-armed them ([Adding a node](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#adding-a-node>)). Delete them to force new ones. Each node's SSH host key is generated there too, installed by Ignition and listed in `output/known_hosts`, which the playbooks' SSH options trust alone (`StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`); a rebuilt node keeps its key and nothing is trusted on first contact. The private halves are as sensitive as the token. The installer keeps its copy of the node config `0600` in RAM; `flatcar-install` carries that mode to the OEM partition.

## Node hardening

`ansible/templates/kubeadm.yaml.j2` and `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2` carry the settings below. They land at provisioning time and change only on `make reinstall`.

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `proxy.disabled: true` | Cilium replaces `kube-proxy`. `kubeadm upgrade apply` reads the field from the `kubeadm-config` ConfigMap; a `skipPhases` on init leaves `proxy: {}` stored, and every upgrade restores `kube-proxy` |
| `--kubelet-certificate-authority` | The API server verifies the kubelet's serving certificate for exec, logs, attach and port-forward, the calls that carry command output. `serverTLSBootstrap` has the kubelet request its certificate from the cluster CA, and [kubelet-csr-approver](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/index.md>) approves it |
| `--admission-control-config-file` | A [Pod Security default](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#pod-security-admission>) for namespaces without labels, so a namespace nobody labelled is `baseline`, not `privileged` |
| `--authentication-config` | Anonymous requests reach only `/livez`, `/readyz`, `/healthz` (the kubelet's probes, `make reinstall`) and `kube-public/cluster-info`, which `kubeadm join` reads before it holds a credential. The file replaces `--anonymous-auth`, which must stay unset |
| `--profiling=false` on the API server, controller-manager and scheduler | `/debug/pprof` exposes internals; CIS asks for it off |
| Metrics listeners on the node address | etcd's plain-HTTP metrics and the controller-manager and scheduler bind the node's own address, where Prometheus scrapes them, instead of every interface. The address differs per node, so it comes from per-node JSON patches in `/etc/kubernetes/patches`, which also move the probes; etcd keeps `127.0.0.1` for its own |
| `DenyServiceExternalIPs` | `spec.externalIPs` lets whoever can create a Service claim traffic to any node address, unchecked. Nothing here uses it. `NodeRestriction` is repeated because the flag replaces kubeadm's default list |
| `--tls-cipher-suites` and `--tls-min-version`, `tlsCipherSuites` and `tlsMinVersion` | Go's defaults include CBC and 3DES suites; the list keeps the ECDHE AEAD ones. TLS 1.3 ignores the list; the floor stops a downgrade. The kubelet's listener on 10250 gets the same |
| `shutdownGracePeriod` and `shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods` | A `systemctl reboot` outside [Kured's drain](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#rebooting-a-node>), or an ACPI power-off, waits while pods get their SIGTERM window instead of dying mid-write |
| `protectKernelDefaults: true` | The kubelet refuses to start unless `vm.overcommit_memory`, `vm.panic_on_oom`, `kernel.panic` and `kernel.panic_on_oops` are already right. `/etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf` sets them; without the drop-in a fresh node never joins |
| `kernel.panic` with `kernel.panic_on_oops` | An oops reboots the node within seconds instead of wedging it, so Ceph and etcd recover without a power-cycle |
| `seccompDefault: true` | A pod without a seccomp profile runs `RuntimeDefault`, not unconfined; a privileged pod stays unconfined; a running node needs it in the `kubelet-config` ConfigMap too |
| `kernel.dmesg_restrict` and `kernel.kexec_load_disabled` | An escaped container cannot read the kernel log or load another kernel; [Kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) reboots with `systemctl reboot`, not kexec |
| `seLinuxOptions.type: spc_t` on kubeadm's static pods | They read the unlabelled `/etc/kubernetes` and start before the [operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-profiles-operator/index.md>) can install a profile |
| `/etc/audit/rules.d/` | SELinux denials and seccomp events reach the journal and [Loki](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>). Flatcar's rules exclude them: the exclude filter drops whatever a rule matches, even a `never` rule |
| `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hardening.conf` | `AllowUsers core`, no keyboard-interactive, no `ssh-rsa`. Flatcar's drop-in appends `ssh-rsa` and sshd keeps a keyword's first value, so this file sorts ahead of it. `core`'s key is `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` |
| `podPidsLimit` | Bounds the PIDs one pod can hold, so a process that stops reaping its children cannot exhaust the node's PID space and take the kubelet with it. |
| `systemReserved`, `kubeReserved` and `evictionHard` memory | The reservations cap `kubepods.slice` below the node's RAM, so a growing pod is OOM-killed in its own cgroup instead of starving systemd-networkd, sshd and the kubelet. A running node needs the same values in the `kubelet-config` ConfigMap, or `kubeadm upgrade node` reverts them |
| `/etc/tmpfiles.d/kubernetes-cis.conf` | kubeadm writes its files 0644 and Cilium creates the CNI directory 0755; CIS wants 0600 and 0700. systemd-tmpfiles applies them at boot and a kubelet `ExecStartPre` before every start. See [Triage 2026-09-20](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/triage-2026-09-20/index.md#infra-the-nodes>) |
| `systemd-sysupdate-reboot.timer` masked | Flatcar's vendor symlink runs it despite a disabled preset. It would reboot behind [Kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) without a drain, and it fails anyway: the default sysupdate component holds only `noop.conf` |
| `noop.conf` in `/etc/sysupdate.d/` | The unsuffixed directory is the default component that `systemd-sysupdate.service` acts on; the no-op transfer keeps that run from failing while the real transfer sits in the `kubernetes.d` component |

## Secrets

Secrets live in [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) and reach workloads as native Kubernetes `Secret` objects through the [External Secrets Operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md>). Nothing sensitive is committed to Git.

- OpenBao is sealed with Shamir and [unsealed by hand](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#unsealing-after-a-restart>), so the key shares are the root of trust for every other secret: keeping fewer than the threshold loses everything.
- No root token is kept: `make bao-init` revokes it once it has created the [operator login](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#operator-credential>), and one is generated from the shares when needed. The operator login reads and writes every KV path, so `output/credentials/` is as sensitive as before, but it cannot change policies or auth methods.
- A workload's namespace reaches only `kv/<namespace>/` in OpenBao; the platform's store refuses every other namespace — see [Kubernetes auth](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#kubernetes-auth>).
- A Kubernetes `Secret` is base64, not encryption. Anyone with `get secrets` in a namespace can read what ESO materialised there. Encryption at rest protects the bytes in etcd, not the API.
- Velero's resource backups hold every `Secret` as plain JSON under the `offsite` bucket's `backup.velero/` prefix, so its keys and RGW bypass encryption at rest; only the volume data is encrypted — see [Velero](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/index.md#repository-password>).

### Encryption at rest

The API server encrypts `secrets` with `secretbox` before they reach etcd (`ansible/templates/kubeadm.yaml.j2`; the key file in `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2`). Without it an etcd backup or stolen disk yields every credential the cluster holds.

| Property | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Provider | `secretbox`, with `identity` listed after it |
| Key | Generated once by `make config` into `output/credentials/encryption_key` and base64-encoded into the config as the `secretbox` key |
| Scope | `secrets` only; ConfigMaps and other resources are unencrypted |
| Distribution | The same key on every control-plane node, written by Ignition to `/etc/kubernetes/enc/encryption-config.yaml` (mode `0600`) |

With `identity` last, new writes are encrypted and Secrets written before it was enabled stay readable but are not rewritten. To encrypt what already exists, once the API servers have restarted:

```bash
kubectl get secrets -A -o json | kubectl replace -f -
```

The key lives in `output/credentials/` beside the kubeadm token and certificate key — that directory is what decrypts etcd. The API servers reload the file on change (`encryption-provider-config-automatic-reload`), so rotating it is a file edit and a rewrite of every Secret, by hand — see [Encryption Key Rotation](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/encryption-key-rotation/index.md>). A KMS provider would remove the key file, at the cost of a dependency the cluster must reach before it can serve Secrets.

## Runtime

[Tetragon](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/tetragon/index.md>) records every exec in every pod and alerts when anything but the control plane reads the cluster's key material. It detects; the one exception kills a container that creates an unprivileged user namespace — see [Enforcement](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/tetragon/index.md#enforcement>). A policy that fails to load on a new kernel watches nothing until its alert fires.

## Audit logging

The API server records who did what, to which object, and whether it was allowed; the `audit` labels of Pod Security Admission need it. Policy, retention and queries are in [Audit Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/audit-logging/index.md>).

## Authorization

**AppProjects constrain the workloads, not the platform.** `payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml` defines them. `infra` allows `sourceRepos: "*"` and every group and kind in every namespace: it is this repository deploying this repository, so a restriction guards against nothing PR review does not. `system` is confined to the `argocd` namespace. `apps` has the boundary to draw, because its Applications come from a second repository with a lighter review: it accepts only the workloads repository and the chart repositories the workloads use, may not write into any platform namespace (`authentik` included, by an admission policy), and at cluster scope may create nothing but namespaces, never at the `privileged` Pod Security level — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#admission-policies>).

**Every platform namespace is default-deny in both directions**, one `CiliumNetworkPolicy` file per namespace plus the cluster-wide rules, and Cilium enforces them: `policyAuditMode` is off, so a flow no rule allows is dropped — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#network-policies>) and [Rollout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#rollout>).

**Pod Security Admission enforces in every namespace but `kube-system`.** Each carries `enforce` at the level it needs and `warn`/`audit` at a stricter one — see [Pod Security Admission](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#pod-security-admission>).

**Image references are checked at admission.** An untagged or `latest` image is refused, and so is a registry outside the allowlist. Signatures are not verified: few of the upstreams sign, so a verifier would exempt nearly everything. See [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#admission-policies>).

**`apps-gateway` admits routes from every namespace** (`allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: All`), so a policy reserves the platform names — see [Route hostnames](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md#route-hostnames>).

## Exposed interfaces

Every platform UI on the infra gateway is behind [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>), and only accounts in `infra-users` get past it. The applications on the apps gateway, some of them public and without Authentik, are listed with their authentication on the [applications repository's pages](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/>). The last two rows are not behind Authentik:

| Service | Authentication | Group required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ArgoCD | Authentik OIDC; local admin disabled. The server runs with `--insecure` because TLS terminates at the Gateway | `infra-users`, then `argocd-admins` or `argocd-viewers` for any access |
| Grafana | Authentik OIDC; login form disabled | `infra-users`; refused without `grafana-admins`, `grafana-editors` or direct `infra-users` |
| Hubble UI | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Rook dashboard | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Prometheus | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Alertmanager | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| OpenBao UI | Token or configured auth method — not behind Authentik | — |
| Agent SSH, `*.ssh.wlkr.ch` | The `ssh` TLS-passthrough listener on `apps-gateway`, which external-dns publishes on the public address. Nothing in front authenticates it: `sshd` in each agent pod admits the user `agent` with public keys only — see [SSH listener](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md#ssh-listener>) and the workloads repository's [Claude agents](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/blob/main/docs/claude-agents.md>) page | — |

The groups and how they nest are in [Groups and roles](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md#groups-and-roles>).

Authentik is a dependency of reaching any of them; the break-glass paths are in [When Authentik is down](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md#when-authentik-is-down>). OpenBao stays out: it holds Authentik's own database password, a loop.

## What would tighten this up

Roughly in order of value against effort:

1. Narrow `sourceRepos` on the AppProjects to this repository and the Helm repositories actually in use.
2. Add a second Alertmanager receiver on a different transport, so a failure of the mail path is not itself unmonitored.
3. Move etcd encryption to a KMS provider, removing the static `encryption_key` in `output/credentials/`.
4. Get a backup copy off the site: TrueNAS pulls the `offsite` bucket to the LAN, which survives losing the cluster but not the site.

See [Known Limitations](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/limitations/index.md>) for the operational counterparts.

# Platform

# Platform

The core infrastructure components that run the cluster, all managed by ArgoCD. Every one of them exists because bare metal does not come with the thing a cloud provider would have handed you: no load balancer, no managed certificates, no block storage API, no identity provider, no backup service.

## Components

One row per directory under `payload/platform/`, with the Application name where it differs from the directory — that is the name `kubectl -n argocd get applications` shows — and the namespace it lands in.

| Component | Namespace | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| alloy | `logging` | Grafana Alloy, the log shipper — see [Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) |
| arc-controller | `arc-systems` | The Actions Runner Controller — see [GitHub runners](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/github-runners/index.md>) |
| [arc-runners](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/github-runners/index.md>) | `arc-runners`, `arc-jobs` | Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, one scale set per repository |
| [argocd](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md>) | `argocd` | ArgoCD itself and the `platform` ApplicationSet |
| argocd-config | `argocd` | The `ExternalSecret` for ArgoCD's OIDC client, and its Grafana dashboard; see [ArgoCD](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md>) |
| argocd-projects | `argocd` | The AppProjects; see [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#structure>) |
| [authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>) | `authentik` | Single sign-on for every platform UI |
| backup | `backup` | Velero's buckets and repository password, the `VolumeSnapshotClass`, the etcd snapshot and defrag and OpenBao snapshot CronJobs, the offsite bucket's policy job and writers, and the backup alerts — see [Backups & Recovery](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md>) |
| [cert-manager](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cert-manager/index.md>) | `cert-manager` | The cert-manager chart |
| certificates | `cert-manager` | The Let's Encrypt issuers and the Gateway wildcard certificates — see [cert-manager](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cert-manager/index.md>) |
| [cilium](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cilium/index.md>) | `kube-system` | CNI, `kube-proxy` replacement, Gateway API, LoadBalancer addresses, WireGuard, Hubble |
| [cloudnative-pg](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md>) | `cnpg-system` | The PostgreSQL operator every workload database runs on |
| [descheduler](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/descheduler/index.md>) | `descheduler` | Evicts pods a drain or reboot left piled on the surviving nodes |
| [external-dns](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-dns/index.md>) | `external-dns` | Publishes Route53 records from HTTPRoutes |
| [external-secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md>) | `external-secrets` | Bridges OpenBao to native Kubernetes Secrets |
| [gateway-api](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>) | `kube-system` | The two Gateways and the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect |
| gateway-api-crds | `kube-system` | The Gateway API CRDs — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>) |
| kube-vip | `kube-system` | Holds the control-plane VIP; adopts the static pod Ignition bootstraps — see [Control Plane VIP](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/index.md>) |
| kubelet-csr-approver | `kubelet-csr-approver` | Approves `kubelet-serving` CSRs against the inventory — see [Metrics Server](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/index.md#verifying-the-kubelet-instead-of-trusting-it>) |
| [kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) | `kured` | Drains and reboots nodes to apply staged OS and Kubernetes updates |
| [logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) | `logging` | Loki's bucket, rules, dashboards and Grafana datasource |
| loki | `logging` | The Loki chart — see [Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) |
| [metrics-server](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/index.md>) | `kube-system` | The `metrics.k8s.io` API behind `kubectl top` and every HPA |
| monitoring, Application `kube-prometheus-stack` | `monitoring`, `node-exporter` | Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, kube-state-metrics; node-exporter alone in `node-exporter` — see [Monitoring](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md>) |
| [openbao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) | `openbao` | Cluster-wide secret store |
| prometheus-operator-crds | `monitoring` | The Prometheus operator CRDs, separate so every chart that ships a `ServiceMonitor` can sync — see [Monitoring](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md#crds>) |
| [rook-ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) | `rook-ceph` | The CSI driver, dashboards and HTTPRoute |
| rook-ceph-cluster | `rook-ceph` | The `CephCluster`, pools and storage classes — see [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) |
| rook-ceph-operator | `rook-ceph` | The Rook operator chart — see [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) |
| security | `kube-system` | Pod Security Admission levels, the network policies and image admission policies — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md>) |
| [security-profiles-operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-profiles-operator/index.md>) | `security-profiles-operator` | Manages SELinux policy modules as `SelinuxProfile` objects; installed, but cannot load one on Flatcar yet |
| snapshot-controller | `backup` | The CSI snapshot controller Velero's volume snapshots need — see [Backups & Recovery](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md>) |
| [tetragon](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/tetragon/index.md>) | `kube-system` | Runtime detection: execs, credential changes and sensitive file reads from the kernel |
| [trivy-operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/trivy-operator/index.md>) | `trivy-system` | Vulnerability, misconfiguration, secret, RBAC and CIS scanning, every finding a CRD |
| [velero](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/index.md>) | `backup` | Volume and resource backups to the Ceph object store |

Across the platform, memory limits are set at roughly 2.5x the measured peak working set and requests at steady state; CPU is requested but never limited. The control-plane static pods take their requests, and the API server a soft `GOMEMLIMIT` so its heap collects before it fills the node, from the kubeadm patches in `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2`; they carry no limits, because a limit on the API server or etcd would OOM-kill the control plane. CoreDNS is kubeadm's too: the same directory holds a patch spreading its replicas one per node, which kubeadm applies at `init` and `upgrade apply` only, and its PodDisruptionBudget sits in the `security` component because nothing else owns a CoreDNS manifest.

## Priority classes

Under memory pressure the kubelet evicts pods over their request first, then the lowest priority; at scheduling, a pod may preempt lower ones unless its class says `Never`. The tiers, the three custom ones in [`priority-classes.yaml`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab/blob/main/payload/platform/security/priority-classes.yaml>):

| Class | Preempts | Who | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system-node-critical` | yes | DaemonSets a node needs: CNI, API VIP, storage, Tetragon | The node is useless without them |
| `system-cluster-critical` | yes | Webhooks, the certificate and secret chain, the CSR approver, Ceph and Rook | Nothing else starts without them |
| `platform-core` | yes | OpenBao, Authentik and its database, Argo CD, Prometheus, Alertmanager | Every app loses its secrets, sign-in or deploys with them; Kured reboots only while Prometheus answers, and alerts need both |
| none (0) | yes | The apps | — |
| `observability` | no | Metrics, logs, backups, Kured, external-dns, the scanner and runner controllers | The largest memory users go before an app, and come back without killing one |
| `batch` | no | Scan jobs, CI runners, CronJobs, agent sessions | Retried on the next run |

The kernel OOM killer ignores priority and goes by QoS class, so a request at steady state matters as much as the class. Outside the platform namespaces the `priority-class-scope` [admission policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#admission-policies>) allows `batch` or no class, so an app cannot outrank the platform.

## Traffic Flow

```
flowchart LR
    NET([Internet]) -->|port-forward 80, 443| R[Router]
    VLAN([Other VLANs, VPN]) --> R
    LAN([LAN]) -->|L2 ARP| APPS[apps-gateway]
    LAN -->|L2 ARP| INFRA[infra-gateway]
    R -->|eBGP route| APPS
    R -->|eBGP route, VLANs only| INFRA
    APPS -->|HTTPRoute| SVC[Service]
    INFRA -->|HTTPRoute| SVC
    APPS -->|proxied app| AK[Authentik outpost]
    INFRA -->|proxied app| AK
    AK -->|authenticated| SVC
    SVC --> POD[Pod]
```

The Gateway addresses are announced twice, over L2 to the flat LAN and over eBGP from the control planes to the router — see [Cilium](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cilium/index.md#configuration>); TLS ends at the Gateway, except on the [`ssh` listener](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md#ssh-listener>), and a [proxied application](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md#integration-styles>) passes through Authentik first. When a hostname stops answering, ask which hop stopped: does the router still hold its BGP routes, does the Gateway still hold its address, does the `HTTPRoute` still say `Accepted`, does the Service still have endpoints.

## HTTPRoute Locations

Routes sit with the component they expose, as a manifest where the component is plain YAML and as chart values where the chart renders its own:

| Service | URL | Route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ArgoCD | `argo.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `server.httproute` in `payload/argocd/values.yaml` |
| ArgoCD CLI (gRPC) | `argo-grpc.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `server.grpcroute` in `payload/argocd/values.yaml` |
| Authentik | `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/authentik/httproute.yaml` |
| Prometheus | `prometheus.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/monitoring/httproute.yaml` |
| Alertmanager | `alertmanager.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/monitoring/httproute.yaml` |
| Grafana | `monitoring.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `grafana.route.main` in `payload/platform/monitoring/application.yaml` |
| Hubble | `hubble.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/cilium/httproute.yaml` |
| OpenBao UI | `vault.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `server.gateway.httpRoute` in `payload/platform/openbao/application.yaml` |
| Rook dashboard | `rook.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/rook-ceph/httproute.yaml` |
| Ceph object store | `s3.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/rook-ceph/httproute.yaml` |
| Home Assistant | `home.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `home-assistant/httproute.yaml` in [homelab-apps](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps>) |

## Deployment

```bash
make bootstrap  # Gateway API CRDs + Cilium, ArgoCD, then the handover
```

After that the `argocd` Application syncs the `platform` ApplicationSet, which generates one Application per `payload/platform/*/application.yaml` plus the `workloads` Application that deploys the `apps` ApplicationSet for the [workloads repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>). Each component directory holds exactly one `application.yaml`; everything else in it is what that Application deploys. [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md>) has the structure and the sync policy.

## Replica placement

Two replicas on one node are not redundancy. Every chart's default is a single `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` anti-affinity term — one weight among the scheduler's scores, which free memory on a larger node outscores. So every component with more than one replica carries an explicit rule:

| Rule | When |
| --- | --- |
| `topologySpreadConstraints`, `maxSkew: 1`, `whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway` | the component runs on the workers only, where a hard rule would leave a replica `Pending` through a Kured drain |
| `podAntiAffinity` `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` | the component tolerates the control planes, so every node is a candidate and a drain always leaves room — or its chart exposes no spread constraint |

Constraints carry `nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor`, so the skew is measured over the nodes the pod can reach rather than over the tainted control planes. Where a component carries a PodDisruptionBudget it says `maxUnavailable: 1`, so a drain or the [descheduler](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/descheduler/index.md>) evicts one replica at a time; `maxUnavailable` rather than `minAvailable`, so a component scaled down to one replica never blocks a drain. Placement is scored once, at scheduling time: pods already sharing a node stay there until something restarts them, and the [descheduler](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/descheduler/index.md>) moves them back only if its evictor is allowed to touch them.

## Rollout order

Nothing enforces an order: every Application syncs as soon as it exists and converges by retry and health, as [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#bootstrap-convergence>) explains. This is the order a fresh cluster settles in, and what each layer is waiting for while it is not yet Healthy.

| Layer | Applications | Waits for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Projects and CRDs | `argocd-projects`, `gateway-api-crds`, `prometheus-operator-crds` | — |
| Network | `cilium`, `kube-vip` | the Gateway API CRDs, see [Cilium](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cilium/index.md#pitfalls>) |
| Controllers | `arc-controller`, `cert-manager`, `cloudnative-pg`, `external-secrets`, `kubelet-csr-approver`, `rook-ceph-operator`, `snapshot-controller` | a network; each brings its own CRDs |
| Storage | `rook-ceph`, `rook-ceph-cluster` | the Rook operator and its CRDs |
| Secrets | `openbao` | `rook-ceph-block` for its volumes, then an operator — see [Bootstrap pauses at OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#bootstrap-pauses-at-openbao>) |
| Certificates | `certificates`, `external-dns` | a working `ClusterSecretStore` and the Route53 credentials in OpenBao |
| Ingress | `gateway-api` | the wildcard certificates the Gateways terminate TLS with |
| Services | `arc-runners`, `argocd-config`, `authentik`, `backup`, `kube-prometheus-stack`, `logging`, `metrics-server` | secrets, storage, the Gateways, and approved kubelet certificates |
| Backends | `loki`, `velero` | the buckets `logging` and `backup` claim |
| Agents | `alloy`, `tetragon` | Loki, so the collector has somewhere to ship |
| Policy | `descheduler`, `kured`, `security`, `security-profiles-operator`, `trivy-operator` | namespaces to label, a Prometheus to scrape and metrics-server for node usage; kured reboots only on a staged update, never on a fresh install |
| Workloads | `workloads` | nothing on its own; the workloads it generates wait for the platform resources they reference — see the [workloads repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>) |

Why the `ClusterSecretStore` sits with OpenBao and the issuers are their own Application is in [Bootstrap convergence](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#bootstrap-convergence>).

# ArgoCD

ArgoCD is the delivery layer, [chosen over Flux](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/decisions/index.md#argocd-with-an-applicationset-not-flux>): everything in `payload/` and in the workloads repository reaches the cluster through it. How the Applications are generated and synced is in [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md>); this page covers the chart values and the supporting resources around ArgoCD itself.

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Namespace | `argocd` |
| Depends on | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) for the OIDC client secret, [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>) for its route, [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>) for every login |
| If it is down | Nothing syncs. Running workloads are unaffected |
| Health check | `kubectl -n argocd get applications` → every one `Synced` and `Healthy` |
| Files | [`payload/argocd/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab/tree/main/payload/argocd>) (Application, `platform` ApplicationSet, `values.yaml`), [`payload/platform/argocd-config/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab/tree/main/payload/platform/argocd-config>) (OIDC `ExternalSecret`, Grafana dashboard), [`payload/platform/argocd-projects/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab/tree/main/payload/platform/argocd-projects>) (AppProjects) |

## Configuration

The parts of `payload/argocd/values.yaml` that are not self-explanatory:

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `redis-ha.image.tag`, `redis-ha.haproxy.image.tag` | Both run ahead of the chart, whose exact patch tags stop being rebuilt once the next one lands and so miss base-image security fixes. Renovate carries them forward; each bare `tag:` must be listed under the `pinDigests: false` rule in `renovate.json` |
| Memory limits, no CPU limits | A CPU limit throttles even on an idle node; memory is not compressible. Sizing is in [Platform](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/index.md>) |
| `metrics.enabled` | Creates the `<component>-metrics` Services whose names are the `job` label the vendored dashboard filters on. The ServiceMonitors render only once the Prometheus operator CRDs exist, so `make install-argo` still works first |
| `configs.params` `server.insecure: true` | TLS terminates at the Gateway. The chart reads this parameter, not `extraArgs`, to point its route at the plaintext port |
| `server.httproute` | The chart renders the `HTTPRoute` to `argocd-server`, so it is not a file of its own; the response-header filters are the same every UI route carries — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md#usage>) |
| `resource.customizations` for `HTTPRoute`, `GRPCRoute` and `PushSecret` | The API server defaults fields no manifest sets: a route's backend `group`, `kind`, `weight` and catch-all `matches`, a `PushSecret`'s `conversionStrategy`. Without the ignore list each object is permanently OutOfSync. Only the catch-all value is ignored, so a changed path still syncs |
| `resourceExclusionsAdditional` for the ARC runner CRs | The runner controller creates and deletes them per job; appended, so the chart's default exclusions stay too |
| `dex.enabled: false` | `oidc.config` talks to [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>) directly, so the chart's bundled Dex would be a second login service with nothing behind it; the redirect URI is the server's own `/auth/callback` either way |
| `notifications.enabled: false` | Nothing is configured to notify, and the controller's ClusterRole reads every Secret in the cluster |
| `admin.enabled: "false"` | With SSO in front, a shared admin password would bypass it with no audit trail |
| `resource.customizations.health.argoproj.io_Application` | Restores health assessment for `Application` resources, dropped in ArgoCD 1.8, so `argocd` reports the health of the ApplicationSet rather than a permanent Healthy |
| `policy.default: ""` | An authenticated user with no matching Authentik group gets no access, not read-only-everything |
| `timeout.reconciliation` and the ApplicationSets' `requeueAfterSeconds` | ArgoCD listens on a private address, so GitHub's webhook cannot reach it and a commit waits for the next poll. The two run separately: the first refreshes Applications, the second re-reads the generator paths. The repo-server caches a revision for the first, so it must not exceed the second or a new commit's files stay invisible to the generator until the cache expires |

The OIDC client ID and secret come from `kv/authentik/config`, the same OpenBao path Authentik's blueprint reads. `argocd-cm` refers to them as `$argocd-oidc:client-id`; ArgoCD resolves a `$name:key` reference only against a Secret labelled `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: argocd`, which the `ExternalSecret` template sets.

The Grafana dashboard in `grafana-dashboards.yaml` is upstream's `examples/dashboard.json`, unmodified, at the ArgoCD version the chart deploys. Renovate does not see it: re-copy it when ArgoCD moves a minor version.

## Usage

### Projects

The `apps` project lists the repositories its Applications may pull from in `payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml`. An OCI Helm chart is listed and referenced **without** the `oci://` scheme (`ghcr.io/janwelker/charts` as `sourceRepos` entry and as the Application's `repoURL`, with `chart:` naming the chart): Argo CD compares the two strings after normalising, and treats a `repoURL` with no scheme as OCI, so a public registry needs no repository Secret and no `enableOCI`. The `default` project Argo CD creates on install is declared in the same file with empty lists: it cannot be deleted, so an Application that names no project lands there and must be able to do nothing.

### Agent account

The `claude` account is the in-cluster Claude Code agents' API identity. It may read everything `role:readonly` reads, `argocd app get --refresh` included, and nothing else: the sessions investigate and open pull requests, and every Application syncs itself. It has `apiKey` only, so it cannot log in. A session with `argocd.enabled` reads its own copy at `kv/claude-<session>/argocd`; only `homelab` has one.

The token has no expiry, so nothing breaks unattended and a leak lasts until rotation. To rotate:

1. Generate the token, logged in through Authentik:

   ```bash
   argocd account generate-token --account claude
   ```
2. Store it with `make bao-secrets`, at `kv/claude-homelab/argocd` (`token`).
3. [Force a sync](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md#usage>) of the `claude-homelab-argocd` `ExternalSecret` in `claude-homelab`; the wrapper reads the mounted file on every call, so no pod restarts.
4. Revoke the previous token; `argocd account get --account claude` lists the IDs with their expiry (a token showing none predates this policy):

   ```bash
   argocd account delete-token --account claude <id>
   ```

The agents reach Argo CD on 443 through the CLI host from [CLI access](<#cli-access>), which resolves to `infra-gateway`'s own address. The caller's policy has to admit both legs, as for any name the Gateway serves ([Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#network-policies>)):

| Leg | Admitted by |
| --- | --- |
| Agent pod to the Gateway address | A name rule for the CLI host: the datapath classifies the Gateway's address as `world`, not `ingress` |
| The Gateway's Envoy to `argocd-server` | An egress rule to the `argocd-server` pod itself. Envoy checks the caller's egress policy again against the pod it picked and answers `403 Access denied` when no rule matches, audit mode or not. The server's own policy already admits the `ingress` entity |

The `homelab` session's policy in the workloads repository carries both. The chart's own policy has only the name rule ([claude-agent\#3](<https://github.com/JanWelker/claude-agent/issues/3>)), so any other session with `argocd.enabled` gets a 403 on every call.

### CLI access

The `argocd` CLI talks gRPC, which the browser route cannot carry: Cilium's Gateway translates gRPC-web into native gRPC, and native gRPC needs an HTTP/2 backend, which the plain `http` port is not. The chart therefore adds an `h2c` port (`http2`, 81) and a `GRPCRoute` on `argo-grpc.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch`, a hostname of its own so the browser route stays as it is.

The Gateway offers no ALPN, and gRPC clients refuse TLS without it, so the CLI needs ALPN enforcement off:

```bash
export GRPC_ENFORCE_ALPN_ENABLED=false
argocd login argo-grpc.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch --sso --grpc-web
```

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n argocd get applications
```

An Application stuck `OutOfSync` has exhausted its [retries](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#sync-policy>) and waits for a hand sync; `ArgoCDApplicationOutOfSync` in [Monitoring](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md#alerting>) mails it.

## Pitfalls

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The local admin is disabled; Authentik is the login**
>
> With Authentik down there is no way into the UI. The break-glass path is a pull request that re-enables `admin.enabled`, since selfHeal reverts a `kubectl patch`; the steps are in [When Authentik is down](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md#when-authentik-is-down>).

## Recovery

### Reinstalling the chart

ArgoCD manages ArgoCD, and the ApplicationSet that deploys the cluster sits inside that same Application. When ArgoCD has synced a config that breaks it, from the deployment host:

1. Reinstall the chart.

   ```bash
   make install-argo
   ```
2. Re-apply the ApplicationSet.

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f payload/argocd/applicationset-platform.yaml
   ```
3. Check that the Applications come back.

   ```bash
   kubectl -n argocd get applications
   ```

# Authentik

[Authentik](<https://goauthentik.io/>) is the cluster's identity provider. Every platform UI sits behind one login instead of a chart-default password each — and Hubble UI, which ships no authentication at all, would otherwise publish every network flow in the cluster to anyone who could reach the hostname.

| Service | Authentication |
| --- | --- |
| ArgoCD | OIDC, local admin **disabled** |
| Grafana | OIDC, login form disabled |
| Home Assistant | Proxy outpost **in front of** its own login — see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>) |
| Umami | Proxy outpost **in front of** its own login; the tracker paths pass through — see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>) |
| Rook dashboard, Hubble UI, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Flowscape, Extractor admin UI | Proxy outpost |
| Wollbi-Fescht, Wollbi Adventsfenster | OIDC for the Payload editors, bound to `wollbi-editors` rather than `infra-users`, see [Groups and roles](<#groups-and-roles>) |

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Namespace | `authentik` |
| Depends on | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) for its OIDC client secrets, [CloudNativePG](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md>) for the database, [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) under it |
| If it is down | Every platform UI loses its only login — see [When Authentik is down](<#when-authentik-is-down>) |
| Health check | `kubectl -n authentik get pods,clusters` → server and worker Ready, `authentik-db` healthy |
| UI | `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` |
| Files | [`payload/platform/authentik/`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab/tree/main/payload/platform/authentik>) |

## Configuration

### Integration styles

**OIDC**, for applications that can do it themselves: ArgoCD and Grafana map group membership to a role. **Proxy**, for the rest: the hostname resolves to Authentik's embedded outpost, a reverse proxy that authenticates the request and only then forwards it to the backend. It needs nothing from the application and protects exactly as far as nothing else can reach the backend.

```
flowchart LR
    U([Browser]) --> GW[infra-gateway / apps-gateway]
    GW -->|argo, monitoring, OIDC workloads| APP[ArgoCD / Grafana / OIDC workloads]
    APP -.->|OIDC redirect to auth.k8s.wlkr.ch| AK[Authentik]
    GW -->|hubble, rook, prometheus, alertmanager, home, flowscape, analytics, extractor-admin| AK
    AK -->|authenticated| BE[Hubble UI / Ceph dashboard / ...]
```

### One hostname

Authentik answers on `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` only, on `apps-gateway`, which the LAN reaches through the router's local record and the outside through Route53. Every OIDC client and the embedded outpost use that one name.

The outpost sends the browser to its `authentik_host` to authenticate, so that name must resolve wherever a proxied application is reached from. `blueprints.yaml` pins `authentik_host` because the embedded outpost otherwise fills it from `web.base_url` on first start and never updates it.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **A client must never mix names**
>
> The `iss` claim is the hostname the token was issued through. A discovery URI on one name and a redirect on another fails every login with an error that blames the token. Should a second hostname ever come back, pin each client to exactly one.

### Where the proxied routes point

A proxied application's route lives with the application: Hubble's in `payload/platform/cilium/`, Rook's in `payload/platform/rook-ceph/`, Prometheus's and Alertmanager's in `payload/platform/monitoring/`, and Home Assistant's, Flowscape's, Umami's and the Extractor admin UI's in the [workloads repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>), each with `authentik-server` as `backendRef`. Gateway API forbids a cross-namespace `backendRef` unless the target namespace grants it, so `referencegrant.yaml` here allows `HTTPRoute` objects from exactly those namespaces to that Service only. A proxied workload is therefore two pull requests, by design: a workload cannot take itself out from behind the authentication layer on its own.

### Database

`database.yaml` is a CloudNativePG `Cluster` with replicas, backed up as in [Backups](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md#backups>). Every login on every platform UI goes through Authentik, so its database must survive a node drain: with one instance a reboot kills the database; with replicas, the operator's PodDisruptionBudgets hold the drain until it has switched the primary over, a few seconds without a writer. The chart's own Postgres subchart is off — both rules are in [the contract](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md#the-contract>).

The replicas only survive a node loss while they sit on separate nodes, which the operator's own `preferred` anti-affinity does not guarantee — hence the `topologySpreadConstraints` block, under the rule in [Replica placement](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/index.md#replica-placement>).

### Chart values

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `authentik.disable_update_check`, `authentik.disable_startup_analytics` and `authentik.avatars` | Telemetry is switched off in config, not permitted by network policy — the same rule as Grafana, Loki and Alloy. `avatars` only seeds a fresh database: since 2024.2 the setting lives in **System → Settings**, and an existing install keeps calling Gravatar until it is set to `initials` there. Blueprints cannot set it: system settings are an internally managed model, and upstream declined a config-level override in [goauthentik/authentik\#26470](<https://github.com/goauthentik/authentik/issues/26470>) |
| `authentik.web.base_url` | Authentik builds e-mail links and outpost redirects from it and cannot infer it; unset, every admin page shows "The base URL has not been configured". |
| `metrics.enabled` and `metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` | The ServiceMonitor renders only when both are set; the switch alone produces nothing, silently. The worker is scraped too: tasks, outpost state and blueprint runs are measured there |
| `postgresql.enabled: false`, `authentik.postgresql.host: authentik-db-rw` and the `global.env` entry | The database is the `Cluster` above. The password is the one CloudNativePG generated into `authentik-db-app`, read as `AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PASSWORD` from that Secret; it is never copied into OpenBao or Git |
| `server.serviceAccountName` and `automountServiceAccountToken` | The chart applies the switch only with a name set; see [Default ServiceAccount tokens](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#default-serviceaccount-tokens>) |
| `server.topologySpreadConstraints` | The chart's `podAntiAffinity` preset is `soft`, which is not enough to hold the replicas apart — see [Replica placement](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/index.md#replica-placement>). The worker is not replicated and needs none |
| `worker.podAnnotations` `homelab.wlkr.ch/secret-generation` | Bumped whenever `authentik-secrets` or a workload's `authentik-secrets-<workload>` gains a key, so ArgoCD restarts the worker in the same sync — see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>) |
| `worker.volumes` `blueprints-workloads` | Authentik keys a blueprint instance by file path and name; `blueprints.configMaps` would mount the file under a second path and register it twice. The mount path stays `workloads` for that reason |

### Where a blueprint lives

Providers and applications are blueprints, so a rebuild reproduces them. `!Find` resolves objects Authentik ships, `!KeyOf` references another entry in the same blueprint, and `!Env` reads an environment variable, which keeps client secrets out of Git. `blueprints_discovery` runs on worker startup, hourly and on a file watcher, asynchronously, so anything configuring itself against a provider must tolerate it not existing yet.

| What | Lives in | Why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform providers, applications, the outpost | `blueprints.yaml` | Mounted into the worker as a ConfigMap |
| A workload's provider and application | `blueprints-workloads.yaml`, one key per workload | A blueprint has full access to Authentik, so it is reviewed as platform code; the [`authentik-foreign-objects`](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#admission-policies>) policy refuses every Application but `authentik` and `security` here |
| Client credentials | Generated by a `PushSecret` beside their reader — `secrets.yaml` for the platform's, the workload's own `secrets.yaml` for a workload's — and read here by `secrets-<workload>.yaml` | A workload can mint a pair but not register it: the `ExternalSecret` and mount entry here keep SSO onboarding a deliberate two-repository act |
| `secret-generation` | `application.yaml` | A new credential needs the worker restarted |
| The outpost's `providers:` list | `blueprints.yaml` | It replaces one global object; two repositories writing it would overwrite each other |
| `referencegrant.yaml` | Here | A proxied workload's route needs granting from this side |

### One issuer for OpenCloud

OpenCloud's web, desktop, iOS and Android clients are four OIDC clients with IDs fixed by the clients, so four providers in Authentik, each under an application of its own. The server and the native clients verify every token against one issuer, and Authentik derives a provider's issuer from its application slug, so the four would disagree. All four therefore use `issuer_mode: global`, whose issuer is the bare hostname, and the `HTTPRoute` rewrites `/.well-known/openid-configuration` on that hostname to the `opencloud` application's discovery document, which is where OpenCloud and its clients fetch it. The document names the global issuer and the shared endpoints, so it serves the other three providers as well. Nothing else uses the root path: every other provider is found under its slug.

### User settings flow

Dependency-Track keys its accounts on the `preferred_username` claim, so a user who could rename themselves could take over another's account. The `05-user-settings.yaml` blueprint in `blueprints.yaml` therefore gives the default brand its own user settings flow with no username field; a username changes only under **Directory → Users**. It replaces the brand's flow instead of editing the default one because the default blueprint rewrites its own objects on every upgrade, and because the **System → Settings** switch `default_user_change_username` is not a model a blueprint can set.

### Authentication flow

`auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` is reachable from the Internet, and the default authentication flow lets a user without a device in on a password alone. The `06-authentication.yaml` blueprint gives the default brand its own flow out of the default password and login stages, with three additions. It is an own flow for the same reason as the [user settings flow](<#user-settings-flow>): the default blueprint rewrites its own objects on every upgrade.

| Addition | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Authenticator validation with `not_configured_action: configure`; TOTP and WebAuthn as setup stages, static tokens accepted as a device class | A password alone is one leak away from every application, so a user without a device enrols one at the next login instead of being let through. Static tokens are the recovery codes for a lost phone, enrolled afterwards under **Settings → MFA devices**, which is why they are not offered as the first device |
| A deny stage after identification, selected by a reputation policy on the address and the username | Every failed login lowers both scores, so an address or a username below the policy's `threshold` is refused until Authentik's reputation expiry clears it; the password stage's own five-attempt cancel only ends the current attempt. The policy *passes* for a bad score, so it selects a deny stage rather than guarding the flow, and it is evaluated when the stage is reached because the flow's own policies see an anonymous request before the username is known |
| A passkey on the sign-in form: an own identification stage hiding whether the account exists and a WebAuthn validation stage requiring user verification, and a policy on the password and second-factor bindings that skips both after a passkey login | The device and its PIN or biometric are two factors already, so a passkey alone signs in; the username, password and second factor still work beside it. The browser offers only discoverable credentials, so a security key enrolled as a second factor may need enrolling again under **Settings → MFA devices** before it appears. Safari and Firefox do not autofill into the form's shadow DOM, so the identification stage's passwordless flow, `homelab-passkey`, offers the same validation stage behind a link as a modal prompt; it has no reputation stage, because a signature cannot be guessed |

To lift a lockout early, delete the score under **Customization → Policies → Reputation scores**.

### Branding

The sign-in pages show the homelab logo on isometric containers in its colours. `scripts/authentik-branding.py` renders both as SVG into `branding.yaml`, a ConfigMap the server mounts at `/web/dist/custom`, so Authentik serves them itself under `/static/dist/custom/` and the default brand in `06-authentication.yaml` points at those paths.

| Choice | Why |
| --- | --- |
| A ConfigMap, not an upload under **Brands** | An upload lives in Authentik's media storage, outside Git and outside a rebuild |
| SVG for both | The background scales to any viewport; the logo is the PNG from `docs/assets/images/` in a 160 px wide SVG, which fixes its size on the card and keeps it sharp on high-density screens |
| Navy shading at the top and bottom edges of the background | The language picker and "Powered by authentik" are white and sit there; the picker is in a shadow DOM that brand CSS does not reliably reach |

To change either, edit the script, run `uv run python scripts/authentik-branding.py` and commit the regenerated `branding.yaml`. A mounted ConfigMap updates in the running pods within a minute or two, without a restart.

### Bootstrap credentials

Authentik's built-in bootstrap blueprint creates `akadmin` from `AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` only while no `akadmin` exists, and reads nothing from it afterwards. `06-authentication.yaml` then sets the account `is_active: false`: a password-only superuser that never logs in is the one worth guessing, and a disabled one authenticates nowhere. The blueprint touches only `is_active`, so the password and the `authentik Admins` membership stay for break-glass.

Break-glass is `ak shell` from a cluster-admin kubeconfig, which nothing in Authentik can lock out:

```bash
kubectl -n authentik exec deploy/authentik-server -c server -- ak shell -c \
  'from authentik.core.models import User; User.objects.filter(username="akadmin").update(is_active=True)'
```

Then log in with `bootstrap-password` from OpenBao — see [Generated secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#generated-secrets>) — enrol a second factor like any user, and switch the account off again with the same command and `is_active=False`: a blueprint is re-applied only when its file changes, so nothing switches it off for you.

| Variable | Set | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` | Always, from `bootstrap-password` | Without it a fresh install creates `akadmin` with no usable password, and the initial-setup flow that sets one is open to whoever reaches `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` first. Blanking it after the first start buys nothing: the account keeps the password |
| `AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` | Never | It mints a non-expiring superuser API token, `authentik-bootstrap-token`, which nothing here uses, and while the variable is set the blueprint recreates the token whenever it is deleted |

A cluster installed before the token was dropped still holds it: delete `authentik-bootstrap-token` under **Directory → Tokens and App passwords**, once the worker has restarted without the variable.

### Groups and roles

Authorisation is group membership. The blueprints create these groups; membership is set by hand under **Directory → Groups**:

| Group | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `infra-users` | Past the Authentik login of every infra application: ArgoCD, Grafana, Hubble, the Ceph dashboard, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Home Assistant, Flowscape, Umami and the Extractor admin UI. Grafana `Viewer` for a direct member |
| `argocd-admins` | ArgoCD `role:admin`, and `infra-users` |
| `argocd-viewers` | ArgoCD `role:readonly`, and `infra-users` |
| `grafana-admins` | Grafana `Admin`, and `infra-users` |
| `grafana-editors` | Grafana `Editor`, and `infra-users` |
| `wollbi-editors` | A Payload editor on advent.wollbi.ch and fest.wollbi.ch, created on first sign-in; declared in the two sites' blueprints |

Every infra application carries a policy binding to `infra-users`, so an account outside it, such as a wollbi editor's, is refused by Authentik before the application sees it. The four role groups have `infra-users` as their parent, and Authentik counts a child group's members as members of the parent. Grafana only sees the groups a user belongs to directly, and with `role_attribute_strict` it refuses a login that matches none of its three. ArgoCD's `policy.default` is empty, so a user in neither ArgoCD group gets **no** access. The wollbi sites bind `wollbi-editors` instead.

## Usage

### Client secrets

The OIDC client IDs and secrets are generated once into OpenBao and read by both sides — Authentik through `!Env`, ArgoCD and Grafana through their own `ExternalSecret` — so a rebuilt Authentik gets the same credentials and nothing is copied out of a UI.
