# Troubleshooting

## Where to look first

| Symptom | First check |
| --- | --- |
| Secrets missing, certificates not renewing | OpenBao sealed: `bao status` on [every pod](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#health-check>); if so, [unseal](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#unsealing-after-a-restart>) |
| An Application is Degraded, OutOfSync or stuck Progressing | `argocd app get <app>` ([login](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md#cli-access>)), or `kubectl -n argocd get application <app> -o yaml` with Authentik down; a failed sync [retries itself](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#sync-policy>), then needs `argocd app sync <app>` |
| Cannot log in anywhere | [When Authentik is down](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md#when-authentik-is-down>) |
| `kubectl` times out, API unreachable | `kubectl --server https://<control plane>:6443`, then [who holds the VIP](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/index.md#verifying>) |
| `kubectl`: certificate expired | [Control-plane certificates](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/index.md#control-plane-certificates>) |
| A node down or not rejoining | `ssh core@<node> journalctl -u kubelet`; dead for good: [Replacing a failed node](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#replacing-a-failed-node>) |
| Node unreachable after a host firewall change | [Host firewall lockout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#host-firewall-lockout>) |
| `ExternalSecret` not syncing | [External Secrets troubleshooting](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md#pitfalls>) |
| PVCs stuck pending | `ceph status`, then the [Rook dashboard](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) |
| Data deleted, or etcd lost quorum | [Restoring](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md#restoring>), [etcd restore](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md#etcd-restore>) |
| Velero backups failing, repositories NotReady | [Velero recovery](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/index.md#recovery>) |
| The etcd encryption key leaked | [Encryption Key Rotation](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/encryption-key-rotation/index.md>) |
| A hostname stopped resolving to the cluster | Gateway lost its LoadBalancer IP; check the Cilium L2 pool |
| A node will not install, or hangs at a blinking cursor | [Troubleshooting PXE boot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#troubleshooting-pxe-boot>) |
| A node installs but comes up with no OSD | [No OSDs after reprovisioning](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md#no-osds-after-reprovisioning>) |

Alerts are [mailed by Alertmanager](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md#alerting>), but nothing monitors the delivery path, so an empty inbox proves nothing.

## Rolling back a bad sync

The only fix is a revert commit. Under automated sync ArgoCD refuses `argocd app rollback`, a manual sync to an older revision is undone at the next poll, and a patched generated Application is overwritten by the next ApplicationSet reconcile — see [Sync policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#sync-policy>). The exception is `argocd` itself, which is not generated: `argocd app set argocd --sync-policy none` holds a rollback until `syncPolicy.automated` is restored.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Do not fix a broken workload with `kubectl edit`: `selfHeal` puts the manifest back on the next reconcile, leaving no trace of the fix. Change the manifest instead.

# Updates & Upgrades

Three mechanisms update a node, and all three land their changes on disk and wait for a reboot. A node can be four patch releases behind while reporting that everything is up to date.

## OS updates

Flatcar downloads OS updates in the background into the passive half of its A/B partition pair. `locksmithd`, which would normally coordinate the reboot, is masked in `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2`, because a reboot must drain the node first. In its place `flatcar-reboot-sentinel.timer` polls `update_engine_client -status` and touches `/run/reboot-required` once an update is staged. [Kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) consumes that marker: it drains, reboots and uncordons, one node at a time and only while Ceph and etcd are healthy. To move sooner, see [Rebooting a node](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#rebooting-a-node>).

The alerts in `payload/platform/monitoring/node-update-rules.yaml` watch that this happens, because Trivy scans containers and not the host: `NodeRebootPending` when a node carries the marker too long, `NodeOsVersionDrift` and `NodeKubeletVersionDrift` when the nodes disagree, and `ControlPlaneVersionLag` when the kubelets run a version no API server runs.

```bash
make os-release uptime
ssh core@<node> systemctl status update-engine --no-pager
```

## Kubernetes

Kubernetes is a [systemd sysext](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/concepts/index.md#systemd-sysexts>). `systemd-sysupdate.timer` runs an update for it on every fire and touches the same `/run/reboot-required` when a new image is fetched. containerd is part of the OS image and updates with it.

### Nodes are pinned to a minor series

The sysupdate config points at `https://extensions.flatcar.org/extensions/`, not at the boot server, and its `MatchPattern` names the major.minor from `kubernetes_version` in `ansible/inventory.yaml` with only the patch left as the `@v` wildcard — see `ansible/templates/sysupdate_kubernetes.conf.j2`.

Patch releases inside the series are picked up automatically; the next minor is not, because an unattended minor jump leaves kubelets ahead of a control plane that refuses to talk to them. sysext-bakery's floating `kubernetes.conf` would stage that minor on whichever node checks first. The Ignition config inlines the rendered file and `make config` writes it to `output/http/kubernetes.conf` for running nodes.

```bash
ssh core@<node> 'ls -l /etc/extensions/ /opt/extensions/kubernetes/'
ssh core@<node> cat /etc/sysupdate.kubernetes.d/kubernetes.conf   # confirm the MatchPattern is pinned
```

### Patch releases

A patch sysext swaps only kubelet and kubeadm. The control-plane static pods and CoreDNS keep their images until kubeadm moves them; workers Kured reboots first run the newer kubelet meanwhile, which the skew policy allows within a minor.

1. Wait until every control plane reports the new kubelet.

   ```bash
   kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
   ```
2. Upgrade the control plane. `ansible/playbooks/kube-upgrade.yaml` refuses a minor or a control plane still on the old sysext, runs `upgrade apply` on the first, `upgrade node` on the rest, and renews the control-plane certificates on the way.

   ```bash
   make kube-upgrade
   ```
3. `kubectl version` must report the new server. Merge Renovate's `kubernetes_version` bump, or a new node joins on the old patch.

## Upgrading a minor version deliberately

**kubeadm allows one minor at a time.** v1.34 to v1.37 is three passes through this procedure, each with its release notes read. A newly provisioned node installs `kubernetes_version` directly.

The order is upstream's: the first control plane, the other control planes, then the workers, because a kubelet may run older than the API server but never newer. The sysupdate config goes to one group at a time, since Kured reboots in no particular order.

1. Update `kubernetes_version` in `ansible/inventory.yaml`, and `kubernetes_sha256` beside it to the new image's: `make download` refuses a file that does not match.
2. Fetch the new sysext and regenerate the Ignition and sysupdate configs.

   ```bash
   make download && make config
   ```
3. Stage the new sysext on the first control plane only. The sentinel must exist afterwards; stop otherwise.

   ```bash
   scp output/http/kubernetes.conf core@<node>:/tmp/kubernetes.conf
   ssh core@<node> sudo mv /tmp/kubernetes.conf /etc/sysupdate.kubernetes.d/kubernetes.conf
   ssh core@<node> sudo systemctl start systemd-sysupdate
   ssh core@<node> ls /run/reboot-required
   ```
4. Let Kured reboot it, as in [Rebooting a node](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#rebooting-a-node>). The node must come back `Ready` on the new kubelet version; stop otherwise.

   ```bash
   kubectl get node <node> -w
   ```
5. On that node, run the kubeadm upgrade. `--skip-phases addon/kube-proxy` stops a cluster whose stored `kubeadm-config` predates `proxy.disabled` from redeploying `kube-proxy` beside Cilium; `--patches` keeps the static pods' memory requests and CoreDNS's spread constraint.

   ```bash
   sudo kubeadm upgrade apply <version> --skip-phases addon/kube-proxy --patches /etc/kubernetes/patches
   ```

   It must end with `SUCCESS!` and `kubectl version` must report the new server; stop otherwise.
6. Each other control plane in turn: steps 3 and 4, then `kubeadm upgrade node` with the same flags, which has to run the new kubeadm the reboot swapped in and takes the version `upgrade apply` stored. `kubectl get nodes` must show the node `Ready` before the next one.

   ```bash
   sudo kubeadm upgrade node --skip-phases addon/kube-proxy --patches /etc/kubernetes/patches
   ```
7. Each worker in turn: steps 3 and 4, then `kubeadm upgrade node`, which only fetches the new kubelet configuration. Same check before the next.

   ```bash
   sudo kubeadm upgrade node
   ```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Renovate keeps `kubernetes_version`, `flatcar_version` and `syslinux_version` current in `ansible/inventory.yaml`; which bumps automerge is in [Automerge policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md#automerge-policy>).

## Platform components

Everything in `payload/`, ArgoCD included, is upgraded by ArgoCD when a Renovate bump merges. Cilium, the Gateway API CRDs and ArgoCD are installed from the same `targetRevision` before ArgoCD exists — see [Version pins](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#version-pins>).

## Control-plane certificates

kubeadm issues the control-plane certificates for one year and renews them only during `kubeadm upgrade`, so a year without a [patch](<#patch-releases>) or [minor](<#upgrading-a-minor-version-deliberately>) upgrade takes the API servers, the etcd peers and the front proxy down together. The kubelet certificates are the exception: the serving certificate is rotated through [kubelet-csr-approver](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/index.md>) and the client certificate by the kubelet itself.

`payload/platform/monitoring/control-plane-certificate-rules.yaml` warns thirty days ahead on the client certificates the API server sees, which kubeadm issues together with the serving ones; the chart's own `KubeClientCertificateExpiration` takes over at seven days and one day. The renewal is done by hand, once a year or when the alert fires, on every control plane in turn:

1. Read the remaining lifetime; every line but the CA should have well over thirty days.

   ```bash
   ssh core@<control plane> sudo kubeadm certs check-expiration
   ```
2. Renew everything kubeadm issued on that node. The CA is not touched.

   ```bash
   ssh core@<control plane> sudo kubeadm certs renew all
   ```
3. Restart the static pods so they load the new certificates: move the manifests out, wait until `crictl` lists none of the four, move them back. One node at a time, since the API server and etcd on it are down in between.

   ```bash
   ssh core@<control plane> 'sudo mkdir -p /root/manifests-stopped && sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml /root/manifests-stopped/ && until [ -z "$(sudo crictl ps -q --name "kube-apiserver|kube-controller-manager|kube-scheduler|etcd")" ]; do sleep 2; done && sudo mv /root/manifests-stopped/*.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests/'
   ```
4. After the last node, refresh the admin kubeconfig: `admin.conf` was renewed too, and the copy in `output/kubeconfig` carries the old client certificate.

   ```bash
   make kubeconfig
   ```

# Vulnerability Triage

Trivy Operator writes one `VulnerabilityReport` per container, a few thousand findings on a cluster this size. Almost none warrant action, and the work is in proving that quickly. The operator's configuration and failure modes are in [Trivy Operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/trivy-operator/index.md>). This page is the method; the dispositions are in [2026-09-20](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/triage-2026-09-20/index.md>), the Dependency-Track portfolio [2026-09-29](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/triage-2026-09-29/index.md>), platform images [2026-11-21](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/triage-2026-11-21/index.md>).

## Pulling a report

```bash
kubectl get vulnerabilityreports -A -o json > vr.json
jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace as $ns
  | .report.artifact.repository as $img
  | .report.vulnerabilities[]?
  | select(.severity=="CRITICAL")
  | [$ns, $img, .vulnerabilityID, .resource, .installedVersion,
     (.fixedVersion // "NO-FIX"), (.packagePath // .target)]
  | @tsv' vr.json | sort -u
```

## Reading it

- **A missing report is not a clean image.** A failed scan writes nothing; the `TrivyContainerNotScanned` alert reconciles running images against scanned ones continuously.
- **An empty `fixedVersion` means no fix is known, not no problem.** Unfixed findings are kept (`ignoreUnfixed` in `payload/platform/trivy-operator/application.yaml`) because a cluster of them in one base image says the base image is the wrong one.
- **The worst findings are usually not the project's code.** The `target` names the binary, and which binary decides whether anything can be done and by whom.
- **Severity is an opinion, and the two sources hold different ones.** [Dependency-Track](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/dependency-track/>) rates by the advisory's score and Trivy by the distribution's; a finding Trivy has at `UNKNOWN` can be critical there. Use it for which images share a component and for what changed between two tags.
- **Prometheus is not a trend.** It keeps the `retention` in `payload/platform/monitoring/application.yaml`; the daily summary the operator ships to Loki is the history, see [History](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/trivy-operator/index.md#history>).

Two artifacts recur. A `ConfigAuditReport` has no TTL and goes only when its ReplicaSet is garbage-collected, so superseded revisions keep their findings on the dashboard ([aquasecurity/trivy-operator\#3069](<https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-operator/issues/3069>)); when a count looks wrong, check whether the ReplicaSet in the report name still has replicas. `KSV-0125` ("untrusted registry") fires on nearly every container because the check's built-in list is Azure, ECR and GCR, which Trivy Operator does not expose as a parameter; it says nothing about the images.

## Filing policy

Filing goes out under a real name, permanently, and most projects have said what they want:

- **Argo CD** asks in `SECURITY.md` not to raise scanner findings.
- **Home Assistant** (Open Home Foundation) does not accept issues or PRs from autonomous agents.
- **Rook** accepts AI-assisted contributions with disclosure, submitted by a human.
- **Routine Go churn is not a finding.** `grpc` or the stdlib one patch behind is fixed by the next release every project here takes automatically.

"Waiting on release" means the fix is merged upstream and Renovate takes the release when it exists; nothing here speeds it up.

## What is load-bearing

`ConfigAuditReport`, `RbacAssessmentReport` and `InfraAssessmentReport` are fixable here rather than upstream. Two checks are most of the volume: `KSV-0014` (read-only root filesystem) and `KSV-0118` (empty pod-level `securityContext`, whatever the containers set).

| Where | Why it stays |
| --- | --- |
| Cilium, cilium-envoy, kube-vip, the kubeadm static pods, Rook OSDs and mons, node-exporter, Kured | Host network, host PID, privileged and added capabilities are what these do; `pod-security.yaml` enforces `privileged` in those namespaces for this reason |
| `etcd-backup` and `etcd-defrag` CronJobs | Host network, because etcd listens on the node's loopback; root, because the client certificates are `600 root` |
| Velero node agent | Root and capabilities stay: kopia reads every pod volume, whoever owns the files |
| Images that start as root by design (Home Assistant) | `runAsNonRoot` or a read-only root would change how they run; seccomp is set |
| Read-only root on charts that write under `/` at runtime (Grafana sidecars, OpenBao) | The chart or image decides where; guessing costs an outage (\#663) |
| Every critical or high `ClusterRole` | A chart's operator role, or Kubernetes' own `admin`, `edit` and `cluster-admin`; not narrowable without forking a chart — see [Security Posture](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/security/index.md#authorization>) |
| The kubelet unit at 644: `KCV-0069` | Accepted: it ships in the signed, read-only sysext and holds no secret. The kubelet config, the CA certificate and the CNI directory (`KCV-0077`, `KCV-0075`, `KCV-0056`) are set to the CIS modes by the `tmpfiles` rule in `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2`, because kubeadm rewrites them at 644 on every `init`, `join` and `upgrade`; the dispositions are in [Triage 2026-09-20](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/triage-2026-09-20/index.md#infra-the-nodes>) |

# Development

# Development

How to change this repository without surprising the cluster. Manifests live under `payload/` and are applied by ArgoCD; documentation lives under `docs/`; workloads live in [`homelab-apps`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps>).

- **[Contributing](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/contributing/index.md>)**

  ---

  Repository setup, the checks to run, commit conventions, and how the documentation site is built and published.
- **[Adding a Workload](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>)**

  ---

  Deploying a new application, from the ArgoCD Application through to the documentation page the build fails without.
- **[Adding a Platform Component](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-platform-component/index.md>)**

  ---

  A new directory under `payload/platform/`, and everything a component needs before its first sync: the Application, the policies, the pin and the page.
- **[Maintenance](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md>)**

  ---

  The CI workflows, and what Renovate is and is not allowed to merge on its own.

# Adding a Platform Component

A platform component is a directory under `payload/platform/` with exactly one `application.yaml`; the `platform` ApplicationSet turns it into an ArgoCD Application on the next poll. Workloads go in the [other repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>). Why the platform is shaped this way is in [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md>).

## Steps

1. **Create the directory** with a complete `application.yaml` copied from a sibling: the generator copies its labels, annotations, finalizers and `spec` verbatim, so a fragment is not an Application. It carries `project: infra`, like every component except the two that configure ArgoCD itself. Keep the [sync policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#sync-policy>) as it is — every component carries the same one, `retry` included, and a chart that lands before its CRDs stays failed without it.
2. **Pin the version once**, as `targetRevision` in that file. The `Makefile` reads the bootstrap versions out of these manifests and Renovate bumps them there — see [Version pins](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#version-pins>).
3. **Put each resource with what it needs, not with what it configures.** Nothing orders the Applications, so a `ClusterSecretStore` sits with OpenBao and the issuers are their own component — see [Bootstrap convergence](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#bootstrap-convergence>). A resource whose CRD comes from another component gets `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true`. A component with an `ExternalSecret` needs its namespace on the `openbao` list in `payload/platform/openbao/cluster-secret-store.yaml`, or the ExternalSecret reads `denied by spec.condition`. A chart from a new repository needs that host in the repo-server's policy in `payload/platform/security/network-policies/argocd.yaml`, or the Application reads `ComparisonError`.
4. **Label the namespace** in `payload/platform/security/pod-security.yaml` with the Pod Security Admission level it demonstrably needs, one sentence of why next to any `privileged`, and add a `privileged` one to the list in `namespace-privileged-allowed` — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#pod-security-admission>). Then **deny it to workloads**: add `"!<namespace>"` to the `apps` project's destinations in `payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml`, which otherwise lets every workload Application write into it. A `privileged` namespace is the one that matters: the admission policy guards new Namespaces, not deployments into an existing one, so a workload commit could place a host-networked pod on every node.
5. **Write its network policy** as `payload/platform/security/network-policies/<namespace>.yaml`: the `default-ingress` and `default-egress` deny pair plus one policy per workload that needs more, copied from the namespace most like it. New HTTP rules start as `http: [{}]` until the [rollout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#rollout>) has recorded a week of requests.
6. **Expose a UI** with an `HTTPRoute` on `infra-gateway` next to the component, and put it behind Authentik — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md#usage>) and [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>). A route that crosses namespaces needs a `ReferenceGrant` in the target namespace.
7. **Check Renovate sees the pin.** `renovate-coverage.yaml` fails on one it does not; the fixes are in [Manager rules](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md#manager-rules>).
8. **Write the page** under `docs/platform/` with the shared skeleton — intro, At a glance, Configuration, Usage, Health check, Pitfalls, Recovery only with a real runbook — add it to the nav in `zensical.toml` and to the [Components table](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/index.md#components>). The strict build fails on a page the nav does not list.
9. **Open the PR** and run the checks in [Contributing](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/contributing/index.md>). After the merge the Application appears within one polling interval; a Degraded one is usually waiting on a CRD, a Secret or OpenBao — see [Troubleshooting](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/troubleshooting/index.md>).

# Adding a Workload

Workloads live in [`JanWelker/homelab-apps`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps>), not here. The `apps` ApplicationSet generates one ArgoCD Application per `*/application.yaml` in that repository, so adding an application is creating a directory there and pushing it. Why the split exists is in [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#workloads-live-in-a-second-repository>).

## Rules and platform-side changes

Every directory follows the workloads repository's [conventions](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/>), which also list what the platform does without being asked. Two needs reach into this repository first:

| A workload with | Needs here first |
| --- | --- |
| A chart from a new repository | The host in the `apps` project's `sourceRepos` (`payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml`) and in the repo-server's egress policy (`payload/platform/security/network-policies/argocd.yaml`), or the Application reads `ComparisonError` |
| Secrets from OpenBao | Its namespace on the `openbao-apps` list in `payload/platform/openbao/cluster-secret-store.yaml`, then `make bao-policies` — see [Adding a secret](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md#adding-a-secret>) |

## Step 1: Create the directory

```bash
git clone git@github.com:JanWelker/homelab-apps.git
cd homelab-apps
mkdir my-app
```

## Step 2: Write the Application

`my-app/application.yaml`, for an app built from plain manifests:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/manifest-generate-paths: .
spec:
  project: apps
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps.git
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: my-app
    directory:
      exclude: "application.yaml"
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: my-app
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
    retry:
      limit: 10
      backoff:
        duration: 30s
        factor: 2
        maxDuration: 5m
    syncOptions:
      # No CreateNamespace: namespace.yaml below creates it, with the Pod
      # Security labels an implicitly created one would not have.
      - ServerSideApply=true
```

For a Helm chart that also needs manifests of its own, use a `sources` list with the chart in one entry and this repository in another; `dependency-track/application.yaml` is the worked example. The `syncPolicy` is the one every platform Application carries, `retry` included; without it a workload that referenced a platform resource a minute too early stays failed — see [Sync policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#sync-policy>).

## Step 3: Add the manifests

```text
my-app/
├── application.yaml
├── namespace.yaml      # Pod Security labels, sync wave -2
├── database.yaml       # CloudNativePG Cluster, sync wave -1, if it needs one
├── backup.yaml         # its backup stanza, sync wave -2, with the database
├── deployment.yaml
├── service.yaml
├── httproute.yaml      # if you want it reachable
└── networkpolicy.yaml  # CiliumNetworkPolicy, sync wave -2
```

### The namespace

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: my-app
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
  annotations:
    # Pruning a Namespace deletes the PVCs inside it.
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-2"
```

Set `enforce` to what the image demonstrably needs (`restricted` if it runs non-root, `baseline` if not) and leave `audit` and `warn` stricter so the gap stays visible.

### If it needs a database

```yaml
---
apiVersion: postgresql.cnpg.io/v1
kind: Cluster
metadata:
  name: my-app-db
  namespace: my-app
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-1"
spec:
  instances: 1
  smartShutdownTimeout: 15
  enablePDB: false   # one instance only
  storage:
    size: 10Gi
    storageClass: rook-ceph-block
  bootstrap:
    initdb:
      database: my-app
      owner: my-app
  plugins:
    - name: barman-cloud.cloudnative-pg.io
      enabled: true
      isWALArchiver: true
      parameters:
        barmanObjectName: my-app-db
```

`backup.yaml` is the stanza in [Backing up a database](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md#backing-up-a-database>) with the names filled in; the `cnpg-cluster-backed-up` admission policy refuses a `Cluster` without the `plugins` entry. The operator polls each instance on port `8000` from `cnpg-system`, so the network policy below must admit it.

### The network policy

```yaml
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-ingress
  namespace: my-app
  annotations:
    # With the namespace, ahead of the database at -1.
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-2"
spec:
  endpointSelector: {}
  ingress:
    # Within the namespace, and the node for health probes.
    - fromEndpoints:
        - {}
    - fromEntities:
        - host
        - remote-node
    # The Gateway, on the container port behind the Service the HTTPRoute
    # targets: a policy matches the pod's port, not the Service's.
    - fromEntities:
        - ingress
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "8080"
              protocol: TCP
    # Only if a CloudNativePG Cluster is in this namespace.
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: cnpg-system
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "8000"
              protocol: TCP
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-egress
  namespace: my-app
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-2"
spec:
  endpointSelector: {}
  egress:
    # Within the namespace. DNS is not listed: the cluster-wide policy in
    # payload/platform/security/network-policies/ sends every pod's
    # lookups through the proxy, which is what makes toFQDNs work.
    - toEndpoints:
        - {}
    # Every name the application dials, by name. Authentik counts: its
    # hostname resolves to the Gateway's own address, which is world.
    - toFQDNs:
        - matchName: auth.k8s.wlkr.ch
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "443"
              protocol: TCP
---
# Only if a CloudNativePG Cluster is in this namespace: the instance
# manager and the join and initdb Jobs, which lack the podRole label, read
# the API server.
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: database
  namespace: my-app
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-2"
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      cnpg.io/cluster: my-app-db
  egress:
    - toEntities:
        - kube-apiserver
```

Wave `-2` is load-bearing: at the default wave the policy is applied after the `Cluster` at `-1`, which cannot go Healthy until the `cnpg-system` rule exists, so the sync parks at `-1` forever. Drop the `ingress` rule if the Gateway does not reach this workload directly (a namespace fronted by Authentik's outpost takes its traffic from the `authentik` namespace). A Prometheus rule belongs here only with a ServiceMonitor, on that port, with `rules.http`; the shape and the rollout are in [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#network-policies>).

### Exposing it

```yaml
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: my-app
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: Gateway
      name: apps-gateway
      namespace: kube-system
      sectionName: https
  hostnames:
    - "my-app.k8s.wlkr.ch"
  rules:
    - backendRefs:
        - name: my-app
          port: 80
```

DNS and TLS need nothing further — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>).

### Putting a workload behind Authentik

- **It speaks OIDC:** the `oauth2provider` blueprint is a key of `payload/platform/authentik/blueprints-workloads.yaml`; its client credentials come from a `PushSecret` in the workload's directory writing `kv/<app>/config` — see [Generated secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#generated-secrets>); the discovery URI is `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch`.
- **It does not:** add a `proxyprovider` on the embedded outpost, point the `HTTPRoute` at `authentik-server` in the `authentik` namespace, add the namespace to `payload/platform/authentik/referencegrant.yaml`, and allow the outpost to reach the pods in the `authentik-server` egress policy.

Either way it is two pull requests, one here, because a workload must not be able to put itself behind or take itself out from behind the cluster's authentication layer. Details in [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>).

## Step 4: Open the pull request

```bash
git checkout -b feat/my-app
git add my-app/
git commit -m "feat: add my-app"
git push -u origin feat/my-app
gh pr create --fill
```

Once it merges, the ApplicationSet picks the directory up within its requeue interval (`requeueAfterSeconds` in `payload/workloads/applicationset.yaml`), or immediately after **Refresh** on the `apps` ApplicationSet in the ArgoCD UI.

## Step 5: Document it

The page goes in the workloads repository at `docs/my-app.md`, registered in its `zensical.toml` under both `nav` and `plugins.llmstxt.sections`, and published to [homelab-apps.wlkr.ch](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/>); the `--strict` build fails on an unregistered page. It follows the shared skeleton: intro, At a glance, Configuration, Usage, Health check, Pitfalls, and Recovery where a real runbook exists.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and check |
| --- | --- |
| The Application was never generated | Only `*/application.yaml`, one level deep, is read, and a `spec.project` other than `apps` fails the whole set naming the file. Read the controller log (below) |
| The Application exists but will not sync | It has exhausted its retries, on a fresh cluster usually against a platform resource that arrived later than the retry budget. `argocd app sync <app>` — see [Sync policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#sync-policy>) |
| `Synced`, health `Unknown`, workload running fine | A wave is waiting on a resource that will never go Healthy, with a database usually the `cnpg-system` rule or its wave — see [Sync stuck on the database](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/conventions/#sync-stuck-on-the-database>) |
| Pods will not start; events mention a security policy | `enforce` in `namespace.yaml` is stricter than the image needs. Loosen `enforce`, keep `audit` and `warn`, so violations stay in the [audit log](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/audit-logging/index.md>) — see [Pod Security Admission](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md#pod-security-admission>) |
| Login redirects in a loop, or every link is `http://` | Requests arrive from Cilium's Envoy inside the [pod subnet](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/index.md#cluster-layout>) with TLS terminated at the Gateway. Set the application's trusted-proxy and "overwrite protocol" settings |

```bash
# Why an Application was not generated
kubectl -n argocd logs deploy/argocd-applicationset-controller | tail -50
```

# Contributing

A merge to `main` is a deployment: ArgoCD applies `payload/` to real hardware, and there is no staging cluster in between. The checks below exist to make that routine.

## Setup

```bash
uv sync                     # virtualenv and dependencies, including dev tools
uv run pre-commit install   # the same linters CI runs
```

## Checks

```bash
uv run pre-commit run --all-files       # the fast offline checks below, plus gitleaks
```

The same checks, one at a time:

```bash
uv run yamllint --strict -f github .
uv run zensical build --clean --strict        # docs site
markdownlint-cli2 '**/*.md' '!**/.venv' '!.agent'
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .   # python only
uv run scripts/render-charts.py --out output/rendered   # payload only
uv run pytest -q                              # python, payload conventions
cd ansible && uv run ansible-lint             # ansible only
uv run scripts/server-dry-run.py output/rendered        # payload only, kind
make ignition-check                           # ansible only, not in pre-commit
shellcheck -x --severity=warning scripts/*.sh scripts/lib/*.sh   # shell only
actionlint && uvx zizmor .github/workflows   # workflows only
uv run scripts/docs-length.py origin/main   # docs only: no page grows
```

The dry run writes CRDs and policies to its context, so it refuses any but `kind-*`.

`--strict` is what CI uses. A page not registered in `nav` in `zensical.toml` fails the build, deliberately. On a pull request, the `argo-diff-preview` workflow comments the rendered manifest diff; read it, since a three-line values change can render as two hundred lines of different objects. All workflows: [Maintenance](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md#ci-workflows>).

## Make targets

Every target in the `Makefile`, and the page that explains it. The ones that touch the cluster read `output/kubeconfig` (`KUBECONFIG=<file>` picks another).

| Target | Does | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup` | Creates the virtualenv with every tool | [Setup](<#setup>) |
| `download` | Fetches and verifies the Flatcar image, syslinux and the sysexts | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `config` | Renders the Ignition configs, PXE menus and credentials from the inventory | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>), [Ansible](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/ansible/index.md#playbooks>) |
| `ignition-check` | Validates every host's rendered Ignition and kubeadm configs | [Checks](<#checks>) |
| `artifacts` | `download` then `config` | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `serve` | Runs the TFTP and HTTP boot server | [Boot server](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/index.md#boot-server>) |
| `reinstall` | Arms a node (`LIMIT=<node>`) or, after a typed confirmation, every node to wipe and install on its next network boot | [Node Lifecycle](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/index.md#rebuilding-or-repartitioning-a-node>) |
| `reinstall-cancel` | Disarms them again | [Switching back to local boot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/index.md#switching-back-to-local-boot>) |
| `kubeconfig` | Copies the admin kubeconfig to `output/kubeconfig` | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `check-context` | Guard the cluster targets depend on: fails without a kubeconfig |  |
| `bootstrap` | `install-cilium`, `install-argo`, `bootstrap-apps` in one go | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `install-cilium` | Gateway API CRDs and Cilium, at the pinned versions | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `install-argo` | The argo-cd chart, at the pinned version | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `bootstrap-apps` | The AppProjects and the `argocd` Application; ArgoCD owns everything after | [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#setup>) |
| `storage-check` | Walks the Rook chain and binds a test PVC | [Is storage ready?](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md#is-storage-ready>) |
| `bao-init` | Initialises, unseals and configures OpenBao once | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#bootstrap>) |
| `bao-unseal` | Unseals every sealed replica from the key file (`KEYFILE=<file>` picks another) | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#unsealing-after-a-restart>) |
| `bao-policies` | Rewrites ESO's policies and Kubernetes auth roles | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#kubernetes-auth>) |
| `bao-secrets` | Prompts for the typed secrets and writes them | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#bootstrap>) |
| `bao-rotate-root` | Replaces a kept root token with the operator login | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md#operator-credential>) |
| `claude-session-pat` | Stores (`SESSION=<name>`) or removes (`DELETE=1`) one agent session's GitHub token | [Claude agents](<https://homelab-apps.wlkr.ch/claude-agents/>) |
| `untaint`, `taint` | Removes and restores the control-plane taint | [Single-node clusters](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/index.md#single-node-clusters>) |
| `fonts[-check]`, `mermaid[-check]` | Downloads the pinned webfonts or Mermaid, or diffs them against what is committed | [Vendored assets](<#vendored-assets>) |
| `clean-artifacts`, `clean` | Deletes the generated files, or everything under `output/` after asking | [Repository layout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/index.md#repository-layout>) |

## Branches and commits

Branch names are prefixed by area: `docs/`, `feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/`. Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](<https://www.conventionalcommits.org/>):

```text
docs: explain the stack choices and collect the known limitations
fix(bootstrap): repoint the install targets at the files that exist
chore(deps): update helm release kube-prometheus-stack to v89
```

The body explains *why*; the diff already says what.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Do not hand-edit version numbers**
>
> `targetRevision` in the manifests and the versions in `ansible/inventory.yaml` are owned by Renovate — see [Maintenance](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md#renovate>). A hand bump conflicts with, or is reverted by, the next Renovate PR. The bootstrap targets in the `Makefile` read the same `targetRevision` values rather than pinning their own — see [Version pins](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#version-pins>).

## Review

`.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns every path to the repository owner, which requests that review; it is not required, because an author cannot approve their own pull request. What `main` requires is the `ci-ok` check; which Renovate PRs merge on it alone is in [Automerge policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md#automerge-policy>).

`.agent/rules/general-rules.md` holds the standing rules for AI coding agents working here: GitOps only, docs in `docs/`, no hand-edited versions. Keep it in sync when those conventions change.

## Documentation

The site is built with [Zensical](<https://zensical.org/>) from `docs/`, configured in `zensical.toml`, and published to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yaml` at [https://homelab.wlkr.ch/](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/>). It is deliberately not hosted on the cluster, so it stays readable when the cluster is not. The build also writes `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a `.md` twin of every page for LLM clients ([llmstxt.org](<https://llmstxt.org/>)); the sections of `llms.txt` are listed in `zensical.toml` under `plugins.llmstxt`, so a new section in `nav` needs an entry there too.

| Stage | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Build | `docs.yaml` runs `zensical build --clean --strict` on push to `main` |
| Deploy | The workflow drops a `.nojekyll` marker into `site/` (otherwise Pages runs Jekyll, which drops paths it considers private) and pushes `gh-pages` without force, sparing `pr-preview/` |
| Previews | `preview.yaml` publishes every pull request under `pr-preview/`; closing it removes the preview. Its path filter must match `docs.yaml`, because this is the only `--strict` build a PR gets |

Locally:

```bash
uv run zensical serve   # http://localhost:8000, rebuilds on save
uv run zensical build   # one-off build into site/ (gitignored)
```

### Conventions

- Every page is registered in `nav`; cross-references are relative Markdown paths (`platform/openbao.md`, `../quickstart.md`) so they resolve on the site and on GitHub.
- Diagrams use Mermaid fences; the runtime is a [vendored asset](<#vendored-assets>).
- Markdown is linted by `lint-markdown.yaml` and the `markdownlint-cli2` pre-commit hook. `MD046`: a blank line followed by an indented line reads as a code block, so keep `!!!` admonition bodies to a single paragraph. `MD007`: nested lists indent by four spaces.
- Inline HTML is limited to `<div>` (`MD033` in `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`), which the card grids on hub pages need.
- Theme templates are overridden by a same-named file under `overrides/` (`theme.custom_dir`). Currently only `partials/source.html`, which drops the repository-facts call that 404s because this repository publishes no releases.

### Vendored assets

The site serves fonts and Mermaid itself, making no third-party requests:

| Asset | Served from | Pinned in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Inter](<https://github.com/rsms/inter/releases>), [JetBrains Mono](<https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono/releases>) | `docs/assets/fonts/`, declared by `docs/stylesheets/fonts.css` (`theme.font = false`) | `scripts/update-fonts.sh` |
| [Mermaid](<https://www.npmjs.com/package/mermaid>) | `docs/assets/javascripts/`, loaded by `extra_javascript`, which stops the theme fetching it from unpkg.com | `scripts/update-mermaid.sh` |

Licences sit next to the files; Renovate tracks the pins.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **A vendored-asset PR needs a second commit**
>
> Renovate moves the pin but cannot write the files. Check out the branch, run `make fonts` or `make mermaid`, and commit the result. `fonts-check.yaml` runs the matching `-check` target, which fails the branch until that commit arrives and so holds the automerge. Mermaid stays on the theme's major.

# Maintenance

GitHub Actions workflows lint everything; Renovate chases dependencies.

## CI workflows

All in `.github/workflows/`.

| Workflow | Trigger | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lint-ansible.yaml` | `ansible/**` | `ansible-lint` |
| `ignition-render.yaml` | `ansible/**` | `make ignition-check`: `butane --strict`, `ignition-validate` and `kubeadm config validate` on every host's configs |
| `lint-python.yaml` | `boot_server/*.py`, `scripts/*.py`, `tests/*.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` |
| `lint-yaml.yaml` | `**/*.yaml` | `yamllint` |
| `lint-markdown.yaml` | `**/*.md` | `markdownlint-cli2` |
| `docs.yaml` | push to `main` under `docs/**`, `overrides/**`, `zensical.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Builds and publishes the site — [Documentation](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/contributing/index.md#documentation>). Only the deploy job, which runs no dependency code, can push |
| `preview.yaml` | pull requests on the same paths | Publishes a preview under `pr-preview/`, same split as `docs.yaml` |
| `argo-diff-preview.yaml` | pull requests under `payload/**` | Comments the rendered manifest diff against `main`. It mounts the Docker socket for kind; the token is read-only and the runner ephemeral |
| `server-dry-run.yaml` | pull requests under `payload/**` | Applies the rendered payload `--dry-run=server` to a kind cluster with our CRDs and admission policies; `tests/test_conventions.py` checks the documented rules |
| `image-scan.yaml` | pull requests under `payload/**` | Trivy on the images the PR changes; fails on a fixable CRITICAL the replaced image did not carry, so a finding [waiting on a release](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/vulnerabilities/index.md#filing-policy>) does not block the bump towards it |
| `lint-shell-actions.yaml` | `**/*.sh`, `.github/workflows/**` | `shellcheck`, `actionlint`, `zizmor` |
| `docs-length.yaml` | pull requests under `docs/**` | No existing page grows, dated logs aside; a new component takes the `docs-growth` label |
| `renovate-validate.yaml` | `renovate.json` | `renovate-config-validator` |
| `renovate-coverage.yaml` | every path that can hold a pin | Fails on a pin no Renovate manager extracts |
| `secret-scan.yaml` | every pull request | `gitleaks` over the PR's commits, the same version as the pre-commit hook; a manual run scans the whole history |
| `ci-ok.yaml` | every pull request | Waits for every other check and fails if one failed; the only required check, so the others keep their path filters |
| `fonts-check.yaml` | `scripts/update-{fonts,mermaid}.sh`, `docs/assets/{fonts,javascripts}/**` | The committed files match the pins — [Vendored assets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/contributing/index.md#vendored-assets>) |

## Renovate

Configured in `renovate.json`, on top of the shared preset [JanWelker/renovate-config](<https://github.com/JanWelker/renovate-config>), which holds the policy for every repository. Every component gets its own pull request so a failing update never holds up an unrelated one; the only groups are the sets below that must move together.

### Automerge policy

- **The preset's rules:** three days between a release and its PR, patch and minor automerge once `ci-ok` is green, majors open at 19:00 and wait for a human, and security fixes skip both the wait and the schedule. The preset's README says why for each.
- **Cluster-wide charts and workflow actions wait for a human.** Argo CD applies a merge within a minute and these charts hold cluster-wide rights, so no update of them automerges; the list is in `renovate.json`. Cilium's pending patch and each minor get separate PRs, merged in that order, the only [path upstream tests](<https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/operations/upgrade/>).
- **A Kubernetes minor waits for a human.** `kubernetes_version` is walked forward by hand in version-skew order; an automerged minor would provision a kubelet ahead of the API server — see [Upgrades](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/index.md#upgrading-a-minor-version-deliberately>).
- **Pairs that must move together are grouped into one PR:** `prometheus-operator-crds` with `kube-prometheus-stack`, because the CRDs must not lag the operator; `rook-ceph` with `rook-ceph-cluster`, because Rook requires both charts on the same version; and `markdownlint-cli2` in the workflow with its pre-commit hook, because the two must lint alike; `gitleaks` likewise; the `external-snapshotter` tag with the `snapshot-controller` image it pins, because upstream's manifest at a tag names the previous release's image (a third-party image, so the pair waits for a human); the two ARC charts, because the controller deletes a scale set whose chart version differs from its own; the OpenBao chart with the image the snapshot CronJob runs its CLI from, so the CLI never lags the server it snapshots; and every Python pin (`requires-python`, `.python-version`, the `python` images), because `uv sync` fails when they name different minors.
- **Python ranges bump.** `pyproject.toml` declares `>=` ranges, which a new release already satisfies; `rangeStrategy: bump` is what makes Renovate open a PR for the linters and the docs generator at all.
- **Flatcar and Kubernetes bumps change what a newly provisioned node installs, not what a running node runs** — see [Upgrades](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/index.md>).
- **A vendored-asset bump cannot automerge without its second commit:** `fonts-check.yaml` fails on it and `ci-ok` waits for it — see [Vendored assets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/contributing/index.md#vendored-assets>).
- `config:best-practices` pins GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and container images to digests, and collects every pin into one shared `renovate/pin-dependencies` branch.

### Scope

Python (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`), Docker images, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes and ArgoCD manifests, Helm values files (`payload/**/values.yaml`) and pre-commit hooks, the CI npm tools (`.github/tools/package-lock.json`), plus custom regex managers for the versions in `ansible/inventory.yaml`, the pins in `scripts/update-{fonts,mermaid}.sh`, any `# renovate:` annotation, every CloudNativePG `imageName` under `payload/`, the `selinuxd` image digest, and the tools workflows install by name (the diff-preview image, Trivy, kind, Helm). The `Makefile` is not tracked; it reads `targetRevision` from the owning `application.yaml` ([Version pins](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md#version-pins>)). The Kubernetes sysext and the Gateway API CRDs carry a sha256 beside the pin, checked before use and bumped with the version by the `github-release-attachments` datasource.

### Manager rules

A misconfigured manager fails silently: the run succeeds and nothing is checked. `renovate-coverage.yaml` catches that; locally, after `npm ci --prefix .github/tools`:

```bash
uv run --no-project scripts/renovate-coverage.py
```

The rules, each in `renovate.json`:

- **`pre-commit` must be enabled explicitly** (`"pre-commit": {"enabled": true}`); Renovate ships that manager disabled, and a `packageRules` entry for it does nothing on its own.
- **The `helm-values` manager reads only real values files.** An image tag inline in an Application's `helm.valuesObject:` is invisible to it; put a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above so the annotation manager picks it up, or move the values into a `values.yaml`.
- **A custom manager that pins a full image reference needs `autoReplaceStringTemplate`.** Without it the pin cannot be written, and one unwritable pin fails the whole shared pin branch (`Error updating branch:     update failure` on the Dependency Dashboard, the only symptom, since version bumps keep working).
- **A bare Helm `tag:` value goes in the `pinDigests: false` rule.** A tag like `3.4.4-alpine` has no position for a digest; leave one out and the same banner comes back.
- **A two-part version needs a `versioningTemplate`.** The default `semver-coerced` rejects `6.03`, so the dependency is extracted and then dropped before lookup; `syslinux` and the Inter font pin carry a `regex:` versioning.
- **Match the registry's spelling, not the GitHub org's.** The diff-preview image is `dagandersen/argocd-diff-preview` on Docker Hub; a regex on `dag-andersen` matches nothing and reports nothing.
- **Hold a major with a regex, not a range.** `"allowedVersions": "/^17\\./"` is matched before version parsing; a range like `<18` is graded by npm semver, where a three-part tag such as `17.11.1-trixie` parses as a prerelease and is dropped from every range that does not name one. Python is held at 3.14 this way until ansible-core supports 3.15.
- **Check that the currently pinned version passes its own rule.** A filter that excludes what is deployed excludes everything, silently.

## Language statistics

GitHub's language bar comes from [Linguist](<https://github.com/github-linguist/linguist>), which counts bytes of files it classifies as a *language*. YAML and Markdown are excluded by default, so `.gitattributes` marks YAML detectable and the three vendored Grafana dashboards as vendored: their JSON would otherwise be most of the bar. A vendored dashboard added later needs its own line there.
